questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A retail API on Amazon API Gateway invokes a Lambda function that saves the order and then calls a slow fulfillment system before returning. Clients must receive the API response as soon as the order is saved, and any fulfillment call that fails must be retried and then parked for inspection after repeated failures. Which design meets both requirements?
options: Increase the Lambda function timeout so that fulfillment completes before the API response returns to the client.
Have the function enqueue fulfillment work on an SQS queue and return, with a worker and a dead-letter queue handling retries.
Configure a Lambda failure destination on the API Gateway-integrated function so failed fulfillment calls are captured after execution.
Invoke a Step Functions Express workflow synchronously from API Gateway and rely on its retry policy for the fulfillment call.
questions.correct_rationale: An SQS queue decouples the caller from the fulfillment work, and the worker's event source mapping retries failed messages before moving them to a dead-letter queue for inspection.
distractor_rationales: Raising the timeout keeps the client waiting during fulfillment, which violates the immediate-response requirement, and adds no retry.
Failure destinations apply to asynchronous invocations, and this function is invoked synchronously by API Gateway, so the destination is not used.
A synchronous Step Functions start still holds the API connection open; its retries do not apply after the caller has received a response.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options either keep the caller waiting, use a mechanism that does not apply to synchronous invocations, or offer no retry-and-park path.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A video-processing API on Amazon API Gateway invokes a Lambda function that transcodes uploaded files, but large uploads make the API time out while clients wait for the finished file. The product team requires that callers are not left holding a connection during processing, and that no processing run is cut off by a per-invocation execution ceiling. Which design meets both requirements?
options: Raise the API Gateway integration timeout and the Lambda function timeout so large files finish inside one call.
Have API Gateway put upload requests on an SQS queue while the client waits for the worker to finish.
Split the file into chunks and transcode each chunk in a separate synchronous Lambda call from the client.
Return a presigned S3 URL for direct upload, and let an S3 event notification trigger the transcoding function.
questions.correct_rationale: A presigned upload moves the file straight to S3 without holding an API connection, and the S3 event notification starts processing asynchronously, so no single invocation has to finish the whole job.
distractor_rationales: Raising timeouts still keeps the client connected and still exposes the run to the Lambda execution ceiling.
The client still waits on the same connection for the worker to finish.
Chunked synchronous calls keep every chunk on a client-held connection and add client-side orchestration.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options keep a client connection open or add orchestration without removing the synchronous wait.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: An order workflow calls a payment provider that fails intermittently. The workflow must retry the payment with increasing delays between attempts, and after the final attempt it must route the order to a manual-review branch instead of failing the whole run. Which solution meets both requirements?
options: Publish the payment request to an SNS topic and rely on subscriber retry behavior for failed payments.
Put payment requests on an SQS queue and move messages that exhaust delivery attempts to a dead-letter queue.
Model the workflow in Step Functions with a Retry backoff policy and a Catch branch for manual review.
Invoke the payment API from Lambda and use CloudWatch alarms to restart failed invocations.
questions.correct_rationale: Step Functions supports per-state Retry policies with backoff intervals, and Catch can send exhausted executions to a separate manual-review branch.
distractor_rationales: SNS delivers to subscribers but does not run a review branch after the final failed attempt.
A dead-letter queue parks the failed message but does not start a different workflow branch.
Alarm-driven re-invocation is custom recovery logic with no backoff policy and no review branch.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options retry or park the work but cannot branch to manual review after the final failure.

docLinks.title: Handling errors in Step Functions workflows

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: Every object uploaded to a bucket must reach an internal billing function and an external partner endpoint that authenticates requests with an API key header. Consumers must be added or removed without changing the bucket's notification settings. Which design meets both requirements?
options: Create two S3 event notification configurations, one for the billing function and one for the partner endpoint.
Send events to EventBridge, route them to billing by rule, and deliver to the partner via an API destination.
Publish events to an SNS topic with the function and the partner HTTPS endpoint as subscribers.
Put a forwarding function in the bucket's notification configuration that posts to the partner with the API key header.
questions.correct_rationale: EventBridge rules add or remove targets independently of the bucket, and API destinations deliver events to external HTTP endpoints with connection-level authentication such as API keys.
distractor_rationales: S3 notification targets are AWS service destinations, so the external authenticated endpoint cannot be one of them, and each consumer change edits the bucket's configuration.
SNS satisfies the decoupling requirement, but SNS HTTPS subscriptions do not attach caller-supplied authentication headers such as API keys.
Forwarding satisfies the partner requirement but pins that consumer into the bucket's notification settings, which the requirement excludes.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options cannot reach the authenticated endpoint, miss its headers, or couple consumers into the bucket configuration.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A support application must extract entity types such as dates and account references from submitted tickets to route them, and the team has no machine learning expertise. Which approach meets the need without the team building, training, or hosting a model?
options: Call the Amazon Comprehend entity detection API from the application.
Train a custom entity recognition model in Amazon SageMaker from labeled tickets.
Use Amazon Textract to read the ticket attachments.
Use Amazon Rekognition to classify the ticket text.
questions.correct_rationale: Comprehend offers pretrained entity detection through a simple API call, with no models to train or host.
distractor_rationales: Training a custom model requires labeled data and machine learning operations the team does not have.
Textract extracts text from documents and scans; it does not classify entities in existing text.
Rekognition analyzes images and video, not text.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options need ML expertise, read scans instead of text, or analyze the wrong media type.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: A Lambda function must query an RDS database that sits in private subnets with no route to the internet, and the same function also reads objects from S3 and items from DynamoDB. The team wants to avoid adding a component that pays for internet-bound egress capacity the function does not use. Which configuration meets the requirements?
options: Place the function in public subnets and give it a public IP address.
Place the function in the database's private subnets, and add gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB.
Place the function in private subnets and add a NAT gateway for the S3 and DynamoDB calls.
Place the function in public subnets and move the database to a publicly accessible subnet.
questions.correct_rationale: Functions in private subnets reach the database directly, and gateway VPC endpoints let the function reach S3 and DynamoDB over the AWS network without a NAT gateway.
distractor_rationales: A public subnet puts the function on the internet path but gives no route into the private database subnets.
A NAT gateway works but adds a managed component the requirements ask to avoid for these two services.
Making the database publicly accessible defeats the isolation the private subnets provide.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options either cannot reach the database, add a NAT gateway, or remove the database's isolation.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: An API backed by Lambda shows slow first responses on function instances that have just started, because heavy initialization runs on every new instance. The latency objective applies around the clock, including after idle periods. Which change directly removes the wait caused by new-instance initialization?
options: Increase the function's memory size so initialization code runs faster.
Move the heavy initialization into the handler so it is charged as regular execution.
Configure provisioned concurrency so pre-initialized instances serve incoming requests.
Increase the function's reserved concurrency limit to permit additional simultaneous instances.
questions.correct_rationale: Provisioned concurrency keeps a pool of pre-initialized execution environments ready, so requests are served without new-instance initialization delay.
distractor_rationales: Larger memory shortens the initialization delay but the delay still occurs on new instances.
Moving initialization into the handler moves the same wait into every request.
Reserved concurrency limits parallel instances; it does not pre-initialize them.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options shorten, relocate, or widen the delay instead of eliminating initialization on demand.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: A serverless team wants a function's trigger, memory size, and per-stage environment values declared in one file that deploys through CloudFormation, with local testing before release. Which framework fits?
options: The AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM), whose template declares the function and its event sources and deploys through CloudFormation.
A plain SDK script that recreates the function and its event source triggers by individual API calls at each release, with no template kept.
A shared machine image that bakes the function's environment values into an instance that is launched for each deployment.
A config file inside the deployment package that the handler reads at startup to create its own triggers on first run.
questions.correct_rationale: SAM templates declare functions, event sources, and settings, deploy through CloudFormation, and support local invocation before release.
distractor_rationales: Raw SDK scripts rebuild infrastructure by hand and drift between releases.
Baked images serve instance hosting, not function configuration.
A handler cannot reliably create its own triggers on every start.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options hand-build infrastructure, target the wrong compute model, or invert the trigger relationship.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: A standard SQS queue feeds a worker function through an event source mapping. The worker occasionally processes the same order twice after redelivery, and one duplicate caused a double refund. The team must keep the existing queue, and refunds must stay correct even when redelivery happens. What should the team do?
options: Increase the queue's visibility timeout so redeliveries become less frequent.
Switch the application to a FIFO queue so the broker suppresses duplicate deliveries.
Make the worker idempotent with a DynamoDB conditional write on the order ID.
Configure a dead-letter queue so duplicate messages are removed from the source queue.
questions.correct_rationale: Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery, so the consumer must tolerate redelivery; a conditional write keyed on the order ID makes the refund side effect happen once.
distractor_rationales: Longer visibility reduces how often redelivery happens but does not prevent it, and the refund stays incorrect when it occurs.
A FIFO queue changes queue semantics and ordering behavior the team must adopt, and the requirement is to keep the current queue.
A dead-letter queue parks messages after failed attempts; it does not identify duplicates the worker already processed successfully.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options reduce redelivery frequency or change the queue instead of making the side effect idempotent.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: Some requests to a Lambda proxy integration on API Gateway fail with a 502 response, and the logs show 'Malformed Lambda proxy response'. Successful paths return correctly formatted responses. Which change fixes the failing paths?
options: Return a JSON object with statusCode and body from every code path.
Raise the API Gateway integration timeout so responses are not truncated.
Add a request validator to reject the malformed requests at the API boundary.
Enable content negotiation on the integration to translate plain strings automatically.
questions.correct_rationale: A Lambda proxy integration requires the function to return a JSON object with statusCode and body; paths that return something else produce a 502.
distractor_rationales: Timeout truncation produces a different error, and the fast successful paths are the ones failing here.
The requests are valid; the function's response shape is the defect.
There is no setting that converts a plain-string return into the proxy response format.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options change timing, reject valid input, or rely on a feature that does not exist.

docLinks.title: Using Lambda proxy integrations with API Gateway

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A bucket collects application debug logs that are read briefly after upload and then kept for audit for a year before deletion. Storage cost is the main concern after the first weeks. Which feature reduces cost while keeping the logs retrievable for the audit period?
options: Create an S3 lifecycle rule that deletes the logs after 30 days.
Enable S3 Versioning and delete noncurrent versions after one year.
Copy the logs to a second bucket in a cheaper Region each week.
Transition logs to infrequent-access storage by lifecycle rule and expire after one year.
questions.correct_rationale: Lifecycle rules can transition objects to lower-cost storage classes and expire them later, matching the short read pattern followed by a year of retention.
distractor_rationales: Deleting after 30 days breaks the one-year audit retention.
Versioning governs object versions, not storage cost for current objects.
Cross-Region copies double management effort and do not remove the original objects' cost.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options break retention, address a different problem, or add effort without removing cost.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A pricing service reads product records from an RDS database for nearly every request. Reads target individual records by key, the working set is small and stable, and the service must answer in microseconds. The application already tracks when prices change and can refresh cached entries itself. Which addition best fits?
options: Add ElastiCache for Redis in front of the database with a cache-aside pattern.
Add Amazon CloudFront in front of the service's HTTP endpoints.
Add an RDS read replica and point the service's read queries at it.
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator on the tables that back the product records.
questions.correct_rationale: An in-memory Redis cache with cache-aside updates answers keyed reads with very low latency and lets the application refresh entries when prices change.
distractor_rationales: CloudFront caches HTTP responses at edge locations and is not an application-level cache for keyed database reads.
A read replica still serves disk-based queries, which do not reach microsecond latency.
DAX accelerates DynamoDB tables, not records stored in RDS.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options cache the wrong layer, keep disk in the path, or apply to a different database engine.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A game leaderboard must report top scores and player ranks with sub-millisecond reads, and scores change as players finish matches. The team's client library is built on Redis data structures. Which managed service fits the access pattern?
options: Store scores in DynamoDB and scan the table for the top players.
Store scores in S3 and regenerate a static leaderboard file after each match.
Keep scores in ElastiCache for Redis and read top ranks from memory.
Keep scores in an RDS table with an index on the score column.
questions.correct_rationale: Redis sorted sets maintain an ordered collection that reports top members and ranks directly from memory, and ElastiCache runs Redis as a managed service.
distractor_rationales: Scanning a table to find leaders reads every item and does not maintain ranks.
Regenerating a file per match adds write-time work and serves stale ranks between regenerations.
A relational index returns ordered rows, but each rank query is a disk-backed query rather than an in-memory ordered structure.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options scan or regenerate data or answer from disk instead of using an ordered in-memory structure.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A DynamoDB table has ample provisioned capacity, yet writes throttle in bursts that correlate with one tenant's bulk imports. The partition key is the tenant's region name, and all of that tenant's items share it. Which change addresses the throttling at its cause?
options: Redesign the partition key to combine region with a per-item identifier.
Increase the table's provisioned write capacity until the bursts stop throttling.
Add a global secondary index on the region attribute to spread the load.
Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode and accept the bursts.
questions.correct_rationale: Throttling on a low-cardinality partition key is a hot-partition problem; combining the region with a unique per-item attribute distributes writes across partitions.
distractor_rationales: Extra table capacity does not spread a single partition's write load; the same partition remains the bottleneck.
A global secondary index copies data for query patterns; it does not change the base table's partition layout.
On-demand mode changes how capacity is billed and absorbed but does not spread one partition's traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add capacity or indexes without redistributing the write load across partitions.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A checkout flow writes the payment status to DynamoDB and immediately reads it back when a second service requests it. Some reads return the previous status right after a write, and the business rule says the checkout screen must always show the status from the most recent successful write. Reads are otherwise far more frequent than writes. Which change meets the requirement without migrating the data or adding extra writes?
options: Write an empty conditional update after each write to force consistency.
Migrate the checkout records to RDS for read-after-write semantics.
Increase the table's read capacity so reads return the latest value.
Perform the checkout read with strong consistency on the item.
questions.correct_rationale: Strongly consistent reads return the latest write; they can be requested per call, so the checkout read alone changes while other reads stay eventually consistent.
distractor_rationales: A follow-up write does not change read consistency for other requests.
Migrating a database to obtain one read pattern adds cost and rework far beyond the requirement.
Read capacity controls throughput, not whether a read sees the latest write.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add work or capacity without changing what a read can see.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A company's web application must let employees sign in with the corporate SAML 2.0 identity provider, and the app's APIs must accept short-lived tokens issued after that sign-in. The security team rejects managing passwords inside the application. Which configuration fits?
options: Create an IAM user for each employee and issue static access keys to the app.
Federate a Cognito user pool with the corporate identity provider and use the pool's tokens to authorize API calls.
Create a Cognito identity pool that trusts the corporate identity provider and hand out AWS credentials to the app.
Create a Cognito user pool with application-managed user sign-up and no federation.
questions.correct_rationale: A user pool federates SAML sign-in and issues short-lived tokens that the app's APIs accept, so no application-managed passwords are involved.
distractor_rationales: Per-user IAM keys are long-lived static credentials and are not how human sign-in to an application works.
An identity pool exchanges tokens for temporary AWS service credentials; it does not issue the app-facing tokens the SAML sign-in needs.
A non-federated pool makes employees manage separate credentials instead of using the corporate directory.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options issue static keys, solve the wrong layer, or skip federation of the corporate directory.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A web application lets users upload documents directly from the browser to S3. No long-term credentials may exist in the browser, and each upload grant must cover one server-chosen object key and stop working after a short time. Which mechanism fits?
options: Embed an IAM user's access key in the page and scope it with a bucket policy.
Have the backend generate a presigned PUT URL for the server-chosen key with a short expiry.
Configure the bucket for public writes and validate file names after upload.
Issue temporary credentials through a Cognito identity pool to the browser session.
questions.correct_rationale: A presigned URL grants time-limited access to one specific object and needs no credentials in the browser; the server chooses the key and the expiry.
distractor_rationales: An embedded static key is a long-term credential in the browser and violates the requirement directly.
Public write access lets anyone write any key; post-hoc validation cannot prevent the write.
Identity pool credentials are scoped session credentials, but the grant is broader than one expiring object upload.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options put credentials or open access in the browser instead of a per-object expiring grant.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A fleet of EC2 build agents uploads artifacts to S3. The security team requires that no long-lived credentials are stored on the instances and that each fleet's access is limited to the artifact paths it needs. Which solution fits?
options: Store an IAM user's access keys in the AMI and scope them with a bucket policy.
Create a bucket policy that allows uploads from the fleet's public IP addresses.
Attach an IAM role through the instance profile, scoped to the fleet's artifact prefixes.
Rotate the instances' access keys nightly and distribute them with startup scripts.
questions.correct_rationale: An instance profile issues temporary role credentials to the instance automatically, with no stored secrets, and the role's policy scopes access by path.
distractor_rationales: An AMI-embedded key is a long-lived credential stored on the instance, which the requirement excludes.
IP-based trust is fragile as addresses change and does not authenticate the instance itself.
Scripted rotation re-creates the stored-credential problem on every cycle.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options keep long-lived credentials on instances or trust network location instead of the workload.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A deployment pipeline on a hosted CI service must assume an IAM role to deploy to AWS. The security team requires that no cloud credentials are stored in the CI system and that the role is assumable only by pipelines from the team's own repository and branch. Which configuration meets both requirements?
options: Store a dedicated IAM user's long-lived access keys in the CI system's encrypted variables.
Have the pipeline assume a role using keys obtained from AWS STS at run start.
Create an IAM role whose trust policy names the CI service's public IP range.
Create an OIDC provider for the CI and scope role trust to the repository and branch.
questions.correct_rationale: OIDC federation lets the CI exchange its own identity token for AWS credentials, and a trust condition on the token's repository and branch limits who can assume the role.
distractor_rationales: Keys in CI variables are stored cloud credentials, which the requirement forbids.
The pipeline still starts from a stored credential to call STS, so the stored-secret problem remains.
IP-based trust breaks as CI egress addresses change and proves nothing about the source repository.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options keep a stored credential in the pipeline or trust a network attribute that does not identify the workload.

docLinks.title: Creating OIDC identity providers in IAM

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: Users of a Cognito-protected mobile app are logged out by an API that returns 401 roughly an hour after sign-in, while refresh attempts succeed. Product requires that users stay signed in for weeks without re-entering credentials, and that a stolen access token be usable for as short a time as possible. Which change meets both?
options: Set the access token's validity to several weeks in the user pool.
Have the client refresh tokens and send the new access token to the API.
Remove the authorizer from the API so requests are no longer checked for token validity.
Set the refresh token's validity to one hour so every token rotates hourly.
questions.correct_rationale: The refresh token extends the session without re-entry, while short-lived access tokens keep the usable window of a stolen token small.
distractor_rationales: Long-lived access tokens extend the usable window of a stolen token, violating the security requirement.
Removing the authorizer removes authentication entirely.
An hourly refresh token forces re-login constantly, breaking the weeks-long session requirement.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options widen the stolen-token window or break the session-length requirement.

docLinks.title: Using tokens with a user pool

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A document service must encrypt large medical images on the client before upload, and no key material may be embedded in or derived by the application. Decryption must verify the caller's IAM permissions at unwrap time. Which approach fits?
options: Call KMS for a data key, encrypt the image with it, and store the wrapped key beside the object.
Call the KMS Encrypt API on each image and store the returned ciphertext in S3.
Generate an RSA key pair in the browser, encrypt the image, and store the private key in the same S3 bucket.
Configure S3 default encryption with SSE-KMS so objects are encrypted server-side on arrival over TLS.
questions.correct_rationale: Envelope encryption uses a KMS-generated data key for the large payload while the data key itself is protected by KMS, so decryption requires the caller to pass the IAM check at Decrypt time.
distractor_rationales: Passing whole images through the KMS Encrypt API is not the intended pattern for large payloads; KMS is designed to protect data keys.
Storing the private key in S3 leaves the key next to the data and outside IAM control.
S3 server-side encryption happens after the upload and does not satisfy client-side encryption before transfer.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options misuse the KMS API for payloads, store keys beside data, or encrypt at the wrong layer.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A microservices platform reads database credentials at startup from a shared store. An audit requires that credentials rotate automatically on a schedule and that services retrieve the current value without a redeploy. Which solution fits?
options: Store the credentials in Lambda environment variables encrypted with a KMS key.
Keep credentials in an encrypted file in S3 and update it monthly with a scheduled function.
Store the credentials in Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured on a schedule.
Store the credentials in Parameter Store as plain strings and rotate them with the application release.
questions.correct_rationale: Secrets Manager rotates secrets automatically on a schedule through managed rotation functions, and consumers read the current version at runtime.
distractor_rationales: Environment variables are per-function and change with deployment, not on a rotation schedule.
A scheduled file update is custom automation with no managed rotation function or versioning guarantee.
Plain-string parameters are not encrypted and rotation is tied to releases rather than a schedule.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options tie rotation to deployments or hand-roll it without a managed rotation mechanism.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A platform team must enable HTTPS on two custom domains with certificates that renew automatically: one on a regional API Gateway endpoint in eu-west-1, and one on a CloudFront distribution. Where should each ACM certificate be requested?
options: Request both certificates in us-east-1 and attach them to both endpoints.
Request the API's certificate in eu-west-1 and the CloudFront certificate in us-east-1.
Request both certificates in eu-west-1 and attach them to both endpoints.
Request the API's certificate in eu-west-1 and import a self-signed certificate for CloudFront.
questions.correct_rationale: Regional endpoints use certificates from the same Region, while certificates for CloudFront distributions must be requested in us-east-1.
distractor_rationales: A us-east-1 certificate cannot be attached to the regional endpoint in eu-west-1.
The CloudFront distribution cannot use a eu-west-1 certificate.
Self-signed certificates are not trusted by browsers and ACM does not renew them.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options request certificates in the wrong Region or use untrusted certificates.

docLinks.title: HTTPS requirements for custom domains on CloudFront

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: Application log groups contain customer email addresses and phone numbers. Compliance requires that PII is masked when operators read the logs, that the underlying records stay intact for debugging, and that the log groups remain queryable in CloudWatch. Which feature fits?
options: Apply a data protection policy to the log groups to mask the PII.
KMS-encrypt the log groups and restrict decryption to the operators' role.
Have the application replace emails and phone numbers with asterisks before logging.
Export the log groups to S3 and delete them from CloudWatch after masking.
questions.correct_rationale: A data protection policy detects sensitive data patterns in log groups and masks them in console and API output for viewers while the stored records stay intact.
distractor_rationales: Encryption at rest protects stored bytes; it does not mask values shown to authorized readers.
Application-side redaction rewrites the data the team needs for debugging; the policy masks at read time without touching the records.
Exporting and deleting removes the logs from CloudWatch queries.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options protect bytes, destroy data, or move logs out of the query path.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: A customer-facing chatbot built on a foundation model must refuse prompts about a list of disallowed subjects, and any personal information in prompts or responses must be redacted before the transcript is stored. Which mechanism provides both controls as a managed feature?
options: Attach an IAM policy that denies invocations containing disallowed keywords.
Review transcripts nightly with a scheduled Lambda and delete offending messages.
Prompt the model to refuse disallowed subjects and to skip writing personal data.
Create a Bedrock guardrail with denied topics and PII redaction on the model.
questions.correct_rationale: Guardrails evaluate inputs and outputs for denied topics and can redact personal information before responses are stored.
distractor_rationales: IAM policies authorize API calls; they cannot inspect prompt content.
Nightly review leaves disallowed content visible in the meantime and is not a preventive control.
Prompt-based rules are instructions the model may ignore and provide no enforced redaction.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options try to enforce content rules with authorization, after-the-fact review, or prompt instructions.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: A customer chatbot built on a foundation model is drifting off subject when users paste long instructions telling it to ignore its rules and reveal its setup. Which managed control addresses this class of input?
options: Attach an IAM policy that denies invocations whose prompts exceed a length quota.
Tell the model in its system prompt to ignore instructions that try to change its rules.
Create a Bedrock guardrail that applies attack protection to prompts before the model processes them.
Log all prompts and review them weekly for instruction overrides.
questions.correct_rationale: Guardrails include prompt attack protection that filters attempts to override the model's instructions before the model processes them.
distractor_rationales: IAM policies authorize API calls; they do not inspect prompt content.
System-prompt instructions are not an enforced control and the same text asks the model to ignore exactly such instructions.
Weekly review observes abuse after the fact and does not filter inputs.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options authorize, instruct, or review instead of filtering the input.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: An internal agent decides which support actions to take and calls tools that can delete records. Operations requires that destructive tool calls execute after a named approver accepts them and that approvals may take hours to arrive without holding compute open. Which design provides the gate?
options: Grant the agent's IAM role permission to delete records during business hours with a time condition.
Wrap destructive tool calls in a Step Functions task that pauses until the approval flow calls back.
Add a guardrail that blocks any response containing the word 'delete' before it executes.
Run a Lambda function that polls the approval service until approved and then performs the deletion.
questions.correct_rationale: A Step Functions task can pause with a task token until the approval flow calls back, creating a durable, auditable gate before the tool executes.
distractor_rationales: A time condition restricts when deletions happen, not whether a human approved this one.
Keyword blocking on responses does not gate the tool execution and misses paraphrases.
A polling Lambda is a custom, time-limited wait that does not give the durable, hours-long pause the requirement describes.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options constrain timing or content, or replace a durable gate with a polling loop.

docLinks.title: Standard and Express workflows in Step Functions

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: A developer's Lambda function receives AccessDeniedException when invoking a foundation model through the Bedrock Runtime API, although the execution role has bedrock:InvokeModel allowed on the model ARN. The team confirmed the account has not yet enabled use of this model. What must the developer do first?
options: Attach an administrator access policy to the execution role so nothing is denied.
Enable access to the model for the account and Region, then retry.
Create a VPC endpoint for Bedrock so the call is authorized by network path.
Rotate the function's execution role credentials and redeploy the function unchanged.
questions.correct_rationale: Bedrock requires model access to be enabled for the account and Region before invocations succeed; IAM permissions alone do not grant it.
distractor_rationales: Administrator access is excessive and does not address the missing model-access enablement.
A VPC endpoint changes the network path, not the authorization failure.
Rotating credentials does not change what the role is allowed to do.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options change privileges or network paths while the missing piece is service-level access enablement.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: A team's ECR repository holds thousands of images. Images tagged 'prod' must be kept indefinitely, while untagged and superseded build images should be removed automatically. Which feature fits?
options: Create a lifecycle policy that expires images older than 30 days regardless of tag.
Enable registry-level pull-through cache rules so base images are copied on demand.
Run a nightly Lambda that lists images and deletes untagged ones with a manual exception list.
Create a lifecycle policy with tag rules that expires untagged and non-prod images, keeping 'prod' images.
questions.correct_rationale: ECR lifecycle policies apply rules that expire images by tag status and age, keeping production-tagged images indefinitely.
distractor_rationales: Expiring everything older than 30 days deletes the production images the requirement protects.
Pull-through caching controls how external base images are fetched, not how your repository's images expire.
A custom nightly function duplicates built-in automation and depends on a hand-maintained exception list.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options over-delete, address image fetching, or hand-roll built-in automation.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: The same container image must be promoted from development to production unchanged. Environment-specific settings must change without a rebuild, and a bad settings change must roll back through a controlled rollout rather than an instant switch. Which mechanism fits?
options: Externalize the settings to AppConfig and deploy changes with a validated rollout strategy.
Bake the settings into a separate image for each environment before promoting it.
Pass the settings as environment variables set at container start separately in each environment.
Store the settings in Secrets Manager and rotate them on a schedule.
questions.correct_rationale: AppConfig serves environment-specific configuration to the same artifact and deploys changes gradually with validators, supporting rollback during rollout.
distractor_rationales: Per-environment images break the promote-the-same-artifact requirement and rebuild for each change.
Environment variables are fixed at start; changing them requires a restart or redeploy and has no gradual rollout.
Secrets Manager manages credentials, not feature or operational configuration with rollouts.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options rebuild images, require restarts, or misuse a secrets tool for configuration.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: An API on API Gateway mixes Lambda and HTTP integrations. A new release must go to a small percentage of traffic on the same stage and endpoint, with the share adjustable as confidence grows. Which mechanism fits?
options: Use a Lambda alias with weighted routing in front of the production function.
Create a second stage and point selected client groups at its URL.
Enable canary release on the stage, routing a percentage to the new version.
Create weighted Route 53 records pointing at the two API endpoints.
questions.correct_rationale: Stage canary release shifts a percentage of traffic on the same stage regardless of integration type, with the share adjustable at any time.
distractor_rationales: Alias weighting applies only when the integration targets that Lambda alias; the HTTP integrations would not participate.
A second stage changes the endpoint clients call, which the requirement excludes.
Weighted DNS balances at the DNS layer and needs separate endpoints plus client DNS behavior to cooperate.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options cover only Lambda traffic, change the client-facing endpoint, or operate at the DNS layer.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: Forty Lambda functions depend on the same large utility library. Updates to the library must be built once and adopted by each function when its team is ready. Which mechanism fits?
options: Publish the library to CodeArtifact and download it during each function's build.
Package the library as a Lambda layer and update the referenced version.
Copy the library source into each function's repository and sync it weekly.
Build a container image containing the library and run all functions as containers.
questions.correct_rationale: Layers hold shared dependencies versioned separately from function code, and each function chooses the layer version to adopt.
distractor_rationales: CodeArtifact serves package downloads at build time; the dependency still ships inside each function's deployment package.
Copying source into every repository re-introduces forty update points and weekly drift.
Moving to containers changes the deployment model to solve a dependency-sharing problem.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options ship per-function copies or change the compute model.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: A team builds a serverless app with a SAM template. Before deploying to the dev environment, they must run the functions and API locally with production-like event payloads, and the template must stay the single source of truth. Which tool fits?
options: Deploy to a personal development stack in the account and test there.
Write unit tests that mock the SDK calls inside each function.
Invoke the deployed functions from the Lambda console with test events.
Use the SAM CLI to run the app locally from the template.
questions.correct_rationale: The SAM CLI runs functions and serves APIs locally from the SAM template, keeping the template as the single definition.
distractor_rationales: A personal stack is a deployed environment, not local execution, and drifts from the shared template.
SDK mocks test logic, not event payloads, API routing, or the template.
Console test events require a deployment first and exercise the remote function, not local code.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options deploy first, test the wrong layer, or bypass the template.

docLinks.title: What is the AWS SAM framework?

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: A frontend team must build against a working API before the backend exists. The responses for the first endpoints are known JSON shapes, and no backend component may be deployed in that environment. Which approach fits?
options: Deploy a Lambda function that returns the agreed fixture JSON for each route.
Point the frontend at the production API and filter responses client-side.
Run the API on a developer laptop and expose it through a tunnel.
Configure API Gateway mock integrations that return mapping-template responses for each route.
questions.correct_rationale: A mock integration returns a response directly from API Gateway without calling any backend, driven by mapping templates.
distractor_rationales: A fixture function is a deployed backend component, which the environment forbids.
Production data is not the agreed fixtures and pollutes real systems with test traffic.
A tunneled laptop is unavailable to distributed teams and is not a managed environment.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options deploy a component, hit production, or depend on a personal machine.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: A Lambda function behind API Gateway serves production traffic from version 7. A new version must be tested with production traffic pinned to an immutable snapshot, and promotion between versions must not require redeploying code. Which mechanism fits?
options: Point the API at $LATEST and rely on the deployment pipeline to keep it stable.
Deploy two copies of the function and switch the API's integration between them.
Publish version 8 and move the production alias, keeping the API on the alias.
Store a feature flag in Parameter Store and branch inside the function on its value.
questions.correct_rationale: Versions are immutable snapshots and aliases are pointers that can be moved without redeploying, so promotion is a pointer update.
distractor_rationales: $LATEST changes with every deployment and is not an immutable snapshot.
Two functions drift independently and the switch is a redeploy of configuration at best.
A runtime flag changes behavior inside one deployment and does not pin an immutable snapshot.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options expose mutable code, duplicate the function, or flag inside a snapshot.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: An organization's teams publish internal Node.js packages and also install public npm packages. Builds must resolve both from one endpoint, and public packages must be fetchable without publishing them internally. Which service fits?
options: Use CodeArtifact with an upstream repository that proxies npm for internal packages.
Store internal package tarballs in S3 and document the download URLs.
Fork every public package the teams use into an internal git repository.
Push internal packages to the public npm registry scoped by organization name.
questions.correct_rationale: CodeArtifact hosts private packages and pulls public ones through an upstream repository, so one endpoint resolves both.
distractor_rationales: Tarball URLs do not resolve dependency trees or proxy public packages.
Forking every public package multiplies maintenance with no automated updates.
Publishing internal code to a public registry exposes proprietary packages.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options lose dependency resolution, fork everything manually, or leak proprietary code.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: An EC2 application deploys several times a day. Releases must advance in batches across the fleet, roll back automatically when the error-rate alarm fires, and avoid paying for a second fleet of instances. Which deployment approach fits?
options: Blue/green deployment with traffic switching at the load balancer after a smoke test.
All-at-once in-place deployment to every instance, with a manual rollback runbook and no batch boundaries.
Immutable deployment on Elastic Beanstalk with a new fleet for each release.
In-place rolling deployment through CodeDeploy with automatic rollback on the error alarm.
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy in-place deployments advance in batches across instances and support automatic rollback when a CloudWatch alarm fires, without doubling the fleet.
distractor_rationales: Blue/green keeps a full second environment standing, which the cost constraint excludes.
All-at-once exposes the whole fleet immediately and rollback is manual.
Immutable deployments create a new fleet for every release.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options double the environment, expose the fleet at once, or rely on manual recovery.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A pipeline builds once and promotes the same artifact through development, staging, and production. Production promotion requires a named approver's sign-off, recorded with the deploy. Which service configuration fits?
options: Three separate pipelines, each one triggered by its own nightly schedule per environment.
A CodePipeline pipeline with stage-to-stage promotion and a manual approval action before the production stage.
A CodeDeploy application with deployment groups per environment triggered by cron.
A script that copies the artifact between environment buckets and posts a chat message for approval.
questions.correct_rationale: CodePipeline moves a single artifact through stages and supports manual approval actions that record who approved before the next stage runs.
distractor_rationales: Separate pipelines rebuild or re-select artifacts and a schedule is not an approval.
CodeDeploy executes deployments; it does not orchestrate stage progression or record sign-off between environments.
A script has no enforced approval gate or auditable stage model.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options schedule instead of approving, deploy without orchestration, or replace a controlled gate with chat messages.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A team's build produces a Lambda deployment whose dependencies and tooling already live in the team's Dockerfile workflow. The package stays far beyond what a .zip workflow manages comfortably, and the team wants to keep building images as today. Which packaging approach fits?
options: Split the dependencies into Lambda layers and keep the function package as a .zip.
Reduce dependencies until the .zip package is small enough to deploy quickly.
Build the function as a container image and deploy it to Lambda from ECR.
Run the image on ECS instead and call it from Lambda through a queue.
questions.correct_rationale: Lambda accepts container images deployed from ECR, letting the team keep its Docker build workflow for large dependency sets.
distractor_rationales: Layers help share dependencies but do not adopt the existing Docker tooling and still leave a .zip package to manage.
Cutting dependencies to fit a package limit sacrifices the product for the packaging method.
Moving the workload to ECS changes the compute model rather than the packaging.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options keep the zip workflow, shrink the product, or change the compute service.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: Checkout latency spiked in the past week. CloudWatch shows the API's p99 rising, but the request passes through API Gateway, two Lambda functions, and a queue, and the team cannot tell which hop grew. No logs show errors. Which observability change locates the slow hop?
options: Enable X-Ray tracing across the API and functions and compare segment latency.
Raise the log level to DEBUG on every function and re-run the incident.
Add a CloudWatch alarm on the API's p99 metric with a lower threshold.
Query the queue's age-of-oldest-message metric to confirm messages arrive before processing starts.
questions.correct_rationale: X-Ray traces record each segment of a request across the API, functions, and downstream calls, so per-hop latency is directly comparable.
distractor_rationales: Debug logging adds volume and requires correlating lines by hand across four services.
The alarm restates the symptom at a threshold; it does not attribute latency to a hop.
Queue age covers one hop and assumes the queue is the culprit.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add volume, restate the symptom, or inspect a single guessed hop.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: Order messages that fail processing end up in the source queue's dead-letter queue, and the DLQ holds messages whose payloads show an unexpected field that the parser rejects. The fix is deployed. What should the team do with the parked messages?
options: Delete the DLQ and recreate it so the message counters reset to zero.
Leave the messages in the DLQ because future orders will not fail the same way.
Increase the source queue's visibility timeout so in-flight redeliveries pause longer.
Redrive the DLQ messages back to the source queue after confirming the fix.
questions.correct_rationale: A redrive moves parked messages back to the source queue for reprocessing once the defect is fixed, recovering the orders without manual replay.
distractor_rationales: Deleting the DLQ discards the parked orders.
Leaving them abandons recoverable business transactions.
Visibility timeout governs in-flight processing on the source queue, not parked DLQ messages.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options discard, abandon, or address the wrong queue's timing.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: A CodeBuild project fails in the install phase with dependency version conflicts, while the same build succeeds on a developer's laptop. The build log shows one package resolving to a different version than the lockfile on the developer's machine. What is the most direct fix?
options: Switch the build to a larger compute instance class so dependency resolution finishes.
Commit the dependency lockfile so builds install the versions the lockfile pins.
Retry the failed build until the package versions resolve consistently.
Create a custom build image with every dependency preinstalled.
questions.correct_rationale: A committed lockfile pins the resolved dependency versions so the build environment installs exactly what developers see.
distractor_rationales: Instance size does not change which versions are resolved.
Retrying a non-deterministic resolution invites the next drift.
Preinstalling packages hides the drift and grows the image instead of pinning versions.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options change hardware, depend on luck, or mask version drift.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: An incident spans 40 microservices, each with its own log group. The on-call engineer must find which services logged a specific error pattern in the last hour and compare counts per service. Which tool fits best?
options: Create a metric filter on every log group now and wait for data.
Download every log stream and search them with a script running on a developer laptop.
Run a CloudWatch Logs Insights query across the groups for the pattern.
Search the X-Ray service map and traces for the error string.
questions.correct_rationale: Logs Insights queries run interactively across multiple log groups and can group and count matches without pre-defined filters.
distractor_rationales: Metric filters need to exist before the incident and take time to accumulate; they are not ad hoc.
Manual download does not scale across 40 groups during an incident.
X-Ray traces capture request paths and segments, not log text.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options need lead time, do not scale, or search the wrong data type.

docLinks.title: Analyzing log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: A request flows from API Gateway through a Lambda function, an SQS queue, and a worker function. Support must filter all logs for one request's journey and count steps by field without text parsing. Which logging approach fits?
options: Emit structured JSON logs carrying the correlation ID from the request into every hop.
Log plain-text lines with timestamps at every hop and match them by time window.
Set every function's log level to DEBUG and search for the endpoint path.
Store each hop's logs in its own unstructured file and join them manually.
questions.correct_rationale: Structured JSON with a propagated correlation ID lets any tool filter on the exact field for the request across every hop.
distractor_rationales: Time-window matching misjoins concurrent requests and needs text parsing.
DEBUG everywhere raises volume and the endpoint path is shared by many requests.
Manual joins do not support incident-time filtering or counting.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options rely on time, volume, or hand-joining instead of a queryable field.

docLinks.title: Configuring JSON and plain text log formats

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: A platform must emit a latency metric per tenant — thousands of tenants — from a Lambda function, and the metric must appear in CloudWatch without the function making a synchronous metrics call per request. Which approach fits?
options: Call PutMetricData once per request with the tenant as a dimension.
Emit the metric as CloudWatch embedded metric format inside the function's log output.
Create one CloudWatch metric per tenant and increment the right one per request.
Write latency rows to DynamoDB and graph them with an external dashboard.
questions.correct_rationale: Embedded metric format generates metrics from structured log output asynchronously, supporting high-cardinality dimensions without a metrics API call in the request path.
distractor_rationales: A synchronous metrics call per request adds latency and API volume in the hot path.
Pre-creating thousands of single-tenant metrics does not scale and buries the account in metric management.
A database and external dashboard leaves CloudWatch and adds a component to operate.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add a synchronous call, explode metric management, or leave the monitoring product.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: When order-processing messages land in the queue's dead-letter queue, an on-call engineer must be paged within minutes, with no custom code to maintain. Which approach fits?
options: Run a scheduled Lambda that counts DLQ messages and emails a distribution list.
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the source queue's message age and page then.
Check the DLQ's console page at the start of each business day.
Alarm on the DLQ's visible-message count and notify an SNS paging topic.
questions.correct_rationale: SQS publishes queue metrics to CloudWatch, so an alarm on the dead-letter queue's message count can page through SNS without custom code.
distractor_rationales: A scheduled function is custom code and email is not a paging path.
The source queue's age metric fires before messages reach the DLQ and does not indicate failed processing.
Manual checks do not page within minutes.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add custom code, alarm on the wrong queue, or require a human to look.

docLinks.title: Monitoring Amazon SQS queues using CloudWatch

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: A Lambda function's code includes the X-Ray SDK, yet traces show segments only for API Gateway and stop at the function. Tracing settings on the function were left at their default. What is the most direct fix?
options: Enable active tracing on the function so it records a segment.
Deploy the X-Ray daemon as a sidecar process next to the function.
Enable AWS CloudTrail data events for the function's invocations.
Add VPC Flow Logs on the subnets that the function's VPC configuration uses.
questions.correct_rationale: Active tracing on the function makes Lambda record the function's segment and propagate the trace id to the runtime and SDK.
distractor_rationales: Lambda manages tracing for you; a self-run daemon applies to workloads outside Lambda.
CloudTrail records API calls for audit, not request segments.
Flow logs record network traffic, not application traces.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add infrastructure for other workloads or record the wrong kind of data.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Optimize applications by using AWS services and features
questions.question: During traffic spikes, a Lambda function's connections exhaust the RDS instance's connection slots, and the database team has frozen all database-side changes this quarter. The fix must stay at the function level. Which change protects the database while preserving as much throughput as possible?
options: Remove the function's concurrency limit so every spike is fully absorbed by new instances.
Configure provisioned concurrency so pre-initialized instances stay warm between requests.
Set the function's reserved concurrency to a level the database can absorb.
Put RDS Proxy in front of the database and point the function at it.
questions.correct_rationale: Reserved concurrency caps how many execution environments the function can run at once, bounding connections to what the database accepts.
distractor_rationales: Removing the cap lets spikes grow the connection count further.
Provisioned concurrency manages cold starts, not the number of concurrent instances.
RDS Proxy works but adds a new database-side component, which the freeze excludes.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options change speed, warmth, or the database layer while the constraint is the count of concurrent connections.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Optimize applications by using AWS services and features
questions.question: An order system must process each order's messages in sequence — payment, packing, shipping — while different orders proceed in parallel. Which queue design fits?
options: A standard SQS queue with per-message delay settings to enforce order.
A FIFO queue using the order ID as its message group ID.
A single FIFO queue without message groups for all orders.
One standard queue per order, created at checkout and deleted at delivery.
questions.correct_rationale: FIFO message groups preserve order within a group while groups process in parallel, so the order ID as group ID sequences each order.
distractor_rationales: Standard queues do not preserve processing order; delays do not restore sequencing.
A single FIFO queue without groups processes everything one at a time and serializes all orders.
Per-order queues multiply resources and manage queue lifecycle per checkout.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options lose ordering, serialize all orders, or explode queue management.

docLinks.title: Amazon SQS FIFO queue key terms

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Optimize applications by using AWS services and features
questions.question: A DynamoDB table serves read-heavy product lookups. Most reads tolerate brief staleness, a few must see the result of the most recent write, and the team wants microsecond-scale reads with minimal application changes. Which solution fits?
options: Add Amazon CloudFront in front of an API endpoint that reads the table.
Add an RDS read replica and migrate the product data.
Add ElastiCache for Redis and implement cache-aside logic in the application.
Add DAX in front of the table with strongly consistent reads passing through.
questions.correct_rationale: DAX caches DynamoDB reads with minimal code changes, and strongly consistent reads are passed through to the table rather than served from cache.
distractor_rationales: CloudFront caches HTTP responses at the edge, not keyed table items in-process.
DynamoDB does not have read replicas; migrating to RDS is a platform change.
ElastiCache works but requires the application to manage serialization, invalidation, and the cache-aside path — more change than the requirement allows.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options cache the wrong layer, switch platforms, or add application cache logic.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A telemetry pipeline ingests events from thousands of vehicles. Each vehicle's events must be processed in sequence, but different vehicles may be processed in parallel. Which stream design fits?
options: One Kinesis data stream with the vehicle ID as the partition key.
One Kinesis data stream with a random number as the partition key to spread load across shards
A standard SQS queue carrying the vehicle ID as a message attribute for ordering.
One SQS FIFO queue without message groups, so every vehicle shares one processing sequence.
questions.correct_rationale: Kinesis orders records only within a shard, and the partition key decides the shard — the vehicle ID as key sequences each vehicle while shards process in parallel.
distractor_rationales: A random key spreads load but destroys per-vehicle ordering.
Standard SQS queues offer no processing-order guarantee, so an attribute cannot restore ordering.
A FIFO queue without message groups serializes all vehicles one at a time.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options destroy the ordering, rely on a queue that has none, or serialize everything.

docLinks.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams key concepts

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A platform must fan one event stream out to two independent consumers — a real-time fraud check that must not fall behind, and an analytics batch job that reads its inputs later. Delivery to one consumer must not be affected by the other consumer's pace. Which design fits?
options: Use a Kinesis data stream as the source, with each consumer reading the stream at its own pace.
Send events to a single SQS queue that both consumers poll for messages together.
Publish the events to an SNS topic with both consumers registered as push subscribers.
Write events to DynamoDB and have both consumers poll the table with the table's access patterns unchanged.
questions.correct_rationale: A Kinesis stream keeps records available for hours and each consumer holds its own position, so a slow analytics reader cannot delay the fraud check.
distractor_rationales: A shared SQS queue hands each message to exactly one consumer, so both consumers together see each message only once.
SNS delivers pushes to subscribers without independent replay positions, so a slow or failed consumer loses messages rather than catching up later.
Polling a table implements a queue in a database with no ordering or retention semantics and adds read cost to both consumers.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options either share one delivery position, consume destructively, or rebuild a stream in a database.

docLinks.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams key concepts

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: One order-publishing component must notify a shipping service, an analytics function, and an audit function. Each function must receive only the event types relevant to it, and adding a fourth consumer must not change the publisher. Which design fits?
options: Publish to an SNS topic; each consumer's subscription carries a filter policy for its event types.
Publish to an SQS queue and have every consumer poll and ignore irrelevant messages.
Publish to EventBridge and register each new consumer inside the publisher's code path.
Publish three separate SNS topics from the publisher, one topic per consumer.
questions.correct_rationale: An SNS topic decouples the publisher from consumers, and per-subscription filter policies deliver each consumer only its relevant event types.
distractor_rationales: A single queue delivers each message to one consumer, not all three.
Registering consumers in the publisher's code couples them, which adding a consumer must not do.
Per-consumer topics force the publisher to know every consumer and change for each addition.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options share one delivery, couple consumers into the publisher, or explode topics per consumer.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A cleanup function must run every night at 02:00 UTC with no server to keep running between runs. Which mechanism starts it?
options: A scheduled EventBridge rule targeting the function on a cron expression.
A long-running worker process that sleeps until 02:00 and then invokes the function.
A Step Functions state machine with a Wait state of one day.
An SQS queue with a message delayed until the next night.
questions.correct_rationale: EventBridge rules support cron-style schedules that invoke targets at fixed times without any always-on component.
distractor_rationales: A sleeping worker is the always-on server the requirement excludes.
A Wait state still runs a workflow continuously across the day.
A delayed message must be re-sent every day by something that keeps time.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options all keep something running or push the timing problem elsewhere.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A development team wants automated review comments on pull requests that point out likely defects and security issues before a human reviews the change. Which tool provides this in the development workflow?
options: Amazon Q Developer's code review capability in the developers' workflow.
A scheduled CodeBuild run that compiles the code and reports warnings.
CloudTrail logs showing who committed each change to the repository and when
A weekly manual review meeting where developers walk through a shared checklist
questions.correct_rationale: Amazon Q Developer provides AI-assisted code review that flags defects and security issues on changes in the development workflow.
distractor_rationales: A compile run reports build output, not reviewed findings on the change.
CloudTrail records API activity, not code defects.
A manual meeting is the human step the team wants the tool to support, not replace.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options compile, audit, or meet instead of reviewing the change.

docLinks.title: Reviewing code with Amazon Q Developer

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: Uploads to a shared bucket's inbox/ folder must trigger processing, but the compliance team's archive/ folder in the same bucket must never trigger it. Which configuration achieves this?
options: An S3 event notification filtered on inbox/, processor as destination
A lifecycle rule that excludes the archive folder from processing
A Lambda function that runs on every object and checks the folder name before doing work.
Two buckets: one for inbox and one for archive, with notifications on both
questions.correct_rationale: S3 event notifications can filter by prefix, so only inbox/ uploads invoke the destination while archive/ uploads never trigger it.
distractor_rationales: Lifecycle rules manage object expiry and storage class, not event processing.
Running on every object still triggers on archive uploads and spends invocations to decide not to work.
A second bucket adds structure but notifications on both still fire for archive uploads.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options misapply lifecycle rules, invoke anyway, or restructure without filtering.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A queue receives a few messages per minute, and consumers poll continuously with short waits, paying per request for mostly empty responses. Latency of a few extra seconds per message is acceptable. Which setting reduces the request cost?
options: Configure long polling with a maximum wait time so empty responses are less frequent.
Enable FIFO mode on the queue so consumer requests consolidate into fewer calls.
Raise the queue's visibility timeout to its maximum with the queue's delivery semantics unchanged.
Configure a dead-letter queue to absorb empty responses from the polling path.
questions.correct_rationale: Long polling lets the receive call wait for messages to arrive, reducing the number of empty responses and the request charges that come with them.
distractor_rationales: FIFO mode changes ordering and deduplication semantics, not polling cost.
Visibility timeout governs in-flight locking, not empty-poll frequency.
A dead-letter queue handles failed processing, not empty responses.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options change semantics, locking, or failure handling instead of polling behavior.

docLinks.title: Amazon SQS short and long polling

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: An intake endpoint receives form submissions that only need to be appended to an SQS queue for a downstream worker. The team wants no Lambda function between the API and the queue to reduce moving parts, and requests that fail validation must never reach the queue. Which design fits?
options: Configure the endpoint's AWS Service integration to write directly to the queue.
Keep the Lambda proxy integration and have the function write to the queue after validation.
Point the endpoint's HTTP integration at the queue's public HTTPS endpoint URL.
Use a mock integration that records submissions without any backend write.
questions.correct_rationale: API Gateway's AWS Service integration calls the queue directly from the endpoint, removing the intermediary function entirely.
distractor_rationales: A Lambda function between API and queue is exactly the moving part the design removes.
An HTTP integration cannot authenticate to the queue the way the AWS integration does.
A mock integration returns canned responses and writes nothing.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options keep the function, break queue authentication, or write nothing.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: An SQS queue feeds a function through an event source mapping. Processing can take up to two minutes, and the queue's visibility timeout is 30 seconds. Workers report seeing the same message twice and doing the work twice. Which change fixes the duplication?
options: Increase the visibility timeout to exceed the longest expected processing time.
Configure a dead-letter queue with a high maximum receive count for failed deliveries.
Switch the queue to FIFO mode so messages deliver each once.
Reduce the function's memory so processing finishes inside 30 seconds.
questions.correct_rationale: A message becomes visible again while still being processed when the visibility timeout is shorter than the work, causing duplicate processing; the timeout must exceed the longest processing time.
distractor_rationales: A dead-letter queue acts after repeated failed attempts; here the first attempt is still running when redelivery happens.
FIFO queues change ordering and dedup semantics and still rely on visibility for in-flight locking.
Shrinking memory slows processing and widens the gap instead of closing it.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options address failure parking, queue type, or speed while the defect is the timeout-versus-duration gap.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: A function's database endpoint and feature settings differ between environments, and the same deployment package must be promoted without a rebuild. The values are not secret. Which mechanism serves the right values per environment at runtime?
options: Store the values as parameters in Parameter Store, one path per environment.
Bake the values into the package as config files per environment
Store the values in Lambda environment variables and update them on every deployment.
Email the values to the operations team before each promotion to an environment.
questions.correct_rationale: Parameter Store holds environment-scoped values that runtime code reads, so one artifact serves every environment.
distractor_rationales: Per-environment config files recreate the rebuild problem the requirement excludes.
Environment variables are set per deployment and change with it, not with the environment alone.
A manual email is not a runtime configuration mechanism.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options rebuild per environment, redeploy to change values, or rely on manual steps.

docLinks.title: What is Systems Manager Parameter Store?

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: A function consumes an SQS queue with batch size 10 through an event source mapping. One malformed message makes the function throw, and the whole batch fails and redelivers — including nine good messages that were already processed, which then run twice. Processing must not repeat the good work, and the malformed message must not block the batch forever. Which configuration fixes both?
options: Configure the event source for partial batch responses, and add a dead-letter queue for repeated failures.
Set the batch size to 1 so each message fails alone, accepting ten times the invocations
Increase the visibility timeout so the whole batch completes before redelivery begins.
Increase the function timeout so the malformed message eventually parses and succeeds.
questions.correct_rationale: Partial batch responses let the function report per-message success, so only the failing message is retried, and a dead-letter queue parks it after repeated failures.
