distractor_rationales: Batch size 1 stops cross-message repetition but multiplies invocations and does not park the malformed message after failed attempts.
A longer visibility timeout does not change that the whole batch fails together.
A longer function timeout does not make a malformed message succeed.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options shrink, delay, or lengthen instead of reporting per-message success.

docLinks.title: Lambda with SQS: partial batch responses

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: Functions opening a new database connection per invocation exhaust the database's connection slots during bursts. The team wants connection reuse managed without rewriting the applications' query logic. Which service fits?
options: Amazon RDS Proxy, between the functions and the database.
An ElastiCache cluster in front of the database.
A larger database instance class with a higher connection limit.
An SQS queue between the functions and the database.
questions.correct_rationale: RDS Proxy pools and multiplexes database connections, letting many invocations share a smaller set of database connections.
distractor_rationales: ElastiCache caches query results; it does not pool database connections.
A larger instance raises the connection ceiling but still lets bursts exhaust it and does not reuse connections.
A queue changes the invocation model rather than pooling connections.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options cache data, raise limits, or re-architect instead of pooling connections.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: Web session records in DynamoDB must disappear automatically roughly three days after creation, and the team does not want a scheduled cleaner to pay for. Which feature fits?
options: Enable TTL with each item's expiry set three days ahead at write time.
A lifecycle configuration on the table that expires old items automatically each night.
A scheduled function that scans the table and deletes expired sessions every day.
Session records in S3, with lifecycle expiration rules applied to the objects.
questions.correct_rationale: DynamoDB TTL marks items with a per-item expiry timestamp and deletes them automatically after that time, with no scheduled cleaner.
distractor_rationales: Lifecycle configurations are an S3 feature, not a DynamoDB one.
A daily scan runs scan-heavy reads to find what TTL removes automatically.
Moving sessions to S3 changes the access pattern for hot session reads.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options apply the wrong service's feature, add paid cleanup, or move hot data.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A users table keyed by user ID must also answer 'find active users by signup month' efficiently. Most users are inactive, the query filters on an isActive flag plus the signup month, and the team wants to avoid paying storage for index entries of inactive users. Which design fits?
options: A sparse global secondary index holding entries for active users only, by signup month.
Create a global secondary index with partition key signup month and sort key user ID, projected as all attributes, and query it.
Add a new sort key on the base table, rewriting every access pattern that exists.
Scan the whole table monthly and filter the results for active users by signup month.
questions.correct_rationale: A sparse GSI writes index entries only for items that carry the indexed attribute, so marking active users with that attribute keeps inactive users out of the index and its storage.
distractor_rationales: A GSI projecting all users stores entries for inactive users too, paying exactly the storage the team wants to avoid.
Adding a sort key changes the base table's key schema and every access pattern built on it.
A scan reads the whole table monthly and grows with table size.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options scan, index everyone, or restructure the table.

docLinks.title: Working with secondary indexes in DynamoDB

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A transfer operation must decrease one account's balance and increase another's in the same table, and a partial application — one write succeeding without the other — is a business-level defect. Which mechanism provides the guarantee?
options: Two sequential writes with a reconciliation scan afterward.
A DynamoDB transaction that performs both writes in one all-or-nothing operation.
Two parallel writes with an idempotency table for retries.
One write followed by an asynchronous worker that copies the change.
questions.correct_rationale: DynamoDB transactions group multiple writes into a single all-or-nothing commit, so a partial application cannot occur.
distractor_rationales: Sequential writes plus reconciliation detect partial application after the fact instead of preventing it.
Parallel writes race each other and an idempotency table governs retries, not atomicity across two items.
Asynchronous copying accepts the partial state the business rule forbids.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options detect, race, or defer the partial-write problem instead of preventing it.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A billing system generates monthly PDF reports into a private bucket. Customers fetch their own report through the web app, and access must stop working after 15 minutes without any public bucket settings. Which mechanism fits?
options: Make the report objects public and rotate their storage prefixes every month.
The backend generates a presigned GET URL for the customer's object with a 15-minute expiry.
The app's backend fetches the report and streams it through the web server
Copy the customer's report to a public bucket named per customer session
questions.correct_rationale: A presigned GET URL grants time-limited access to one private object and works without any public bucket configuration.
distractor_rationales: Public objects are readable by anyone, not just the customer, regardless of prefix rotation.
Streaming through the app's server funnels every download through backend compute and bandwidth the presigned URL avoids.
A per-session public bucket is public storage with more moving parts and the same exposure.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options make data public, proxy every byte, or multiply buckets.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A mobile app's signed-in users must read and write their own files in S3 directly from the device, and the security team requires that no AWS credentials are stored in the app and that each user's access is limited to their own prefix. Which mechanism fits?
options: A Cognito user pool access token stored in the app and sent to S3 directly.
A Cognito identity pool issuing temporary credentials scoped to the user's own prefix.
An IAM user created per customer, with access keys generated on first login
A public bucket with per-user prefixes and no authentication on the writes.
questions.correct_rationale: Identity pools trade a sign-in identity for temporary AWS credentials, and the role policy can scope access to the user's own prefix via policy variables.
distractor_rationales: A user pool token authenticates to your APIs; S3 does not accept it as an AWS credential.
Per-customer IAM users mean long-lived keys to manage and revoke.
An unauthenticated public bucket has no per-user control at all.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options confuse token types, create long-lived keys, or drop authentication.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A platform team's account hosts shared services. An application in another account must read from its S3 bucket, and the platform team must control exactly which principal can get that access and review it in one place. Which mechanism fits?
options: Create an IAM user in the platform account for the other account's application, and share its keys
An IAM role whose trust policy names the other account's application principal.
A bucket policy that allows anonymous access with a condition on the request's referer header.
Give the other account's root user access through a shared password and username.
questions.correct_rationale: A cross-account role makes the trusted account's principal assume the role for temporary credentials, with the trust policy as the single point of control.
distractor_rationales: A shared IAM user's keys are long-lived secrets that outlive any trust decision.
A referer-header condition is not authentication and anonymous access is public access.
Sharing root credentials is a security incident, not an access design.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options share static secrets, trust headers, or hand over root credentials.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: Engineers run privileged CLI workflows against production. The security team requires that these API calls are only authorized when the engineer's login was confirmed with a second factor in the same session. Which mechanism enforces this?
options: A longer session duration so engineers need to re-authenticate less often overall.
A policy condition requiring the multi-factor authentication claim when the role is assumed.
A dedicated IAM user per engineer with programmatic access keys for the CLI.
IP allowlisting of the office network in the role's trust policy
questions.correct_rationale: A condition on the MFA claim in the trust policy lets STS issue role credentials only for sessions authenticated with a second factor.
distractor_rationales: Session duration changes how often login happens, not whether the second factor is required.
Per-engineer IAM users reintroduce long-lived keys and say nothing about MFA.
Network location does not verify the person's second factor.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options change convenience, credential type, or location while the requirement is the second factor.

docLinks.title: IAM condition keys for multi-factor authentication

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A developer's role can perform kms:Decrypt per its IAM policy, yet decryption of a specific customer-managed key keeps failing with an access denied error. The key exists in the same account and the ARN is correct. What is the missing piece?
options: The developer's role must be recreated with the same name.
The key policy must also allow the role the decrypt action.
The S3 bucket holding the ciphertext must allow the developer's IAM user.
The account must enable model access for KMS in that Region.
questions.correct_rationale: Access to a KMS key requires permission from both sides: the caller's IAM policy and the key's own policy must both allow the action.
distractor_rationales: Recreating a role does not change what either policy allows.
The bucket stores ciphertext; decryption permission is governed by KMS, not the bucket.
Model access is a Bedrock concept and has no role in KMS authorization.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options recreate roles, blame storage, or import concepts from another service.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: An application uses two values. One is a partner account identifier that must be encrypted at rest and changes only when the partner reissues it, about once a year. The other is the master user password of an Amazon RDS DB instance, which must rotate automatically at least every 30 days. The team will not write, deploy, or pay for a rotation function. Which approach meets all of these needs?
options: Both values in Secrets Manager, with automatic rotation scheduled for each value.
The identifier as a Parameter Store SecureString and the password as an RDS-managed rotating secret.
Both values as Parameter Store SecureStrings, each rotated every 30 days by a custom scheduled script.
Both values in Secrets Manager with no rotation configured, updated by hand.
questions.correct_rationale: Parameter Store SecureString suits encrypted configuration values such as account identifiers. RDS can manage the master password in Secrets Manager with managed rotation on a schedule you can modify; managed rotation uses no Lambda function, so nothing is written, deployed, or charged at the Lambda rate.
distractor_rationales: RDS managed rotation covers the password, but scheduled rotation of the partner identifier would need a Lambda rotation function, which the team will not write or pay for.
SecureStrings encrypt both values, but the custom script is rotation code the team will not write or run.
With no rotation configured, the password is not rotated automatically, so the 30-day requirement fails.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options need a Lambda rotation function for the identifier, hand-roll rotation, or skip rotation.

docLinks.title: What is Systems Manager Parameter Store?

Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager - Amazon Relational Database Service

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: An application encrypts records with KMS and must ensure that a data key encrypted for 'purpose=orders' cannot be used by a copy of the application that decrypts records for 'purpose=payroll' — same key, different data domain. Which KMS feature enforces this binding?
options: Separate KMS keys per purpose, with no additional parameter on calls
The encryption context, key-value pairs that must match exactly on decrypt.
A random initialization vector generated per record and stored beside the ciphertext in Amazon S3.
A longer data key length chosen for the payroll domain's records.
questions.correct_rationale: The encryption context is additional authenticated data bound into the encryption; a decrypt call with a different context fails rather than returning plaintext.
distractor_rationales: Separate keys solve the problem differently but do not use the binding mechanism the design already has in one key.
An IV protects against repetition in ciphers; it does not bind ciphertext to a purpose.
Key length is a cipher strength parameter, unrelated to domain binding.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options multiply keys, confuse IVs, or change cipher strength instead of binding the context.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: An AWS service must use a customer-managed KMS key on the application's behalf, and the security team wants this delegation to be scoped, auditable, and revocable without editing the key's policy each time. Which KMS mechanism fits?
options: Embed the key's plaintext key material in the service's configuration files.
A KMS grant on the key for the service's principal and scope.
A wildcard allow statement in the key policy that covers all principals.
Disable CloudTrail logging so the key delegation is not recorded anywhere.
questions.correct_rationale: Grants delegate specific permissions on a key to a principal, can be constrained in scope, and can be revoked without editing the key policy.
distractor_rationales: KMS key material never leaves the service in plaintext; that is not a delegation mechanism.
A wildcard key policy widens access to every principal and is the opposite of scoped.
Disabling logging hides the delegation instead of auditing it.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options leak key material, widen the policy, or hide activity.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A compliance control requires encryption keys to change periodically without re-encrypting stored data or changing application code. Which KMS feature satisfies the control?
options: Export the data monthly and re-encrypt it with a new key offline
Enable automatic key rotation so new material backs the same key ID.
Delete and recreate the KMS key on a fixed schedule each quarter.
Rotate the data keys inside the application and rewrap all stored ciphertexts
questions.correct_rationale: Automatic rotation changes the key's backing material on a schedule while the key ID and stored ciphertext keep working, so applications need no change.
distractor_rationales: Offline re-encryption is a manual pipeline the control asks to avoid.
Deleting and recreating a key breaks decryption of existing data.
Application-side rotation rewraps every stored ciphertext — exactly the work the requirement excludes.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options re-encrypt data, break access, or move the burden into the application.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A team holds TLS certificates for its public endpoints. The security team requires that renewals happen without manual tracking, and that a lapsed certificate cannot silently break a domain. For certificates issued by ACM, which behavior fits?
options: ACM certificates expire after one year and require a new request each year.
The application must re-import the certificate every 90 days from a third party.
ACM renews issued certificates automatically before expiry as long as the domain remains validated.
ACM sends the team a calendar reminder to renew the certificate manually.
questions.correct_rationale: ACM manages renewal of the certificates it issues, renewing them automatically while domain validation holds.
distractor_rationales: ACM-issued certificates renew automatically rather than expiring yearly by policy.
Third-party re-imports apply to imported certificates, not ACM-issued ones.
Manual tracking is exactly what ACM removes for issued certificates.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options describe imported-certificate workflows or manual processes that ACM replaces.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: Before customer support transcripts are sent to a model for summarization, personal information in the text must be detected and removed so it never reaches the model. Which service provides ready-made detection of this content?
options: Amazon Textract to re-read the transcript images.
A regex list maintained by hand for common name patterns.
Comprehend PII detection applied to the transcript first.
AWS Glue to transform the transcripts into another format.
questions.correct_rationale: Comprehend detects personal information in text, so the application can redact it before the transcript reaches the model.
distractor_rationales: Textract reads text out of document images; the transcripts are already text.
Hand-maintained patterns miss formats and drift over time.
Glue transforms data formats and does not identify personal information.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options pattern-match by hand, read images, or reformat instead of detecting PII.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: An AI agent orchestrates several tools: one reads a catalog, one creates tickets, and one deletes records. After a refactor, the agent runs all tools with one broad role, and a reviewer flags that the deletion tool's permissions exceed what it needs. Which change restores the intended security posture?
options: Give the agent's single role administrator access so no tool is ever denied.
Move the deletion tool outside the agent so developers run it by hand.
Scope each tool to its own role, with permissions limited to that tool's actions and resources.
Log every tool call and review the logs each month for excessive use.
questions.correct_rationale: Per-tool roles bound to each tool's actual actions and resources restore least privilege, so the deletion tool cannot do more than delete what it owns.
distractor_rationales: Administrator access removes denials by granting everything, the opposite of least privilege.
Removing the tool changes the product's capability rather than its permissions.
Monthly log review observes excess use after it happens and does not constrain it.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options grant everything, remove functionality, or audit after the fact.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: An audit requires a record of which models the application invoked, when, and with what request identifiers, kept separately from application logs. Which Bedrock capability provides this?
options: A nightly report listing the models enabled for the account and Region.
Reading the application's CloudWatch log groups for recorded prompt text.
Model invocation logging to the destination configured for the account.
The billing console's monthly service totals for the AWS account.
questions.correct_rationale: Model invocation logging records invocation details to a configured destination, separate from application logs, giving the audit its own record.
distractor_rationales: Listing enabled models shows entitlements, not invocations.
Application log groups contain what the app happened to log, not an invocation record.
Billing totals show cost, not call-level activity.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options read app logs, entitlements, or billing instead of an invocation record.

docLinks.title: Model invocation logging in Amazon Bedrock

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: An API receives thousands of malformed payloads daily that the backend rejects anyway, spending compute on requests that could have failed instantly. Which API Gateway feature rejects invalid payloads at the boundary?
options: A Lambda authorizer that inspects each payload before invocation.
A usage plan that limits each client's request rate.
Request validation checking payload shape before the integration runs.
A response mapping template that rewrites backend errors.
questions.correct_rationale: Request validation checks payloads against schemas at the API boundary, rejecting invalid requests before any backend integration runs.
distractor_rationales: An authorizer decides who may call, not whether the payload shape is valid.
A usage plan throttles request volume and says nothing about payload validity.
Response templates act on the way out; the wasted compute happens on the way in.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options police identity, volume, or responses instead of payload shape.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: A containerized service runs on ECS. Operations must define the service's image, port mappings, CPU and memory in one versioned artifact that task runs reference, and updates to that artifact must not require rebuilding the image. Which ECS object fits?
options: The ECS cluster's configuration for the service.
The load balancer's target group for the service
A task definition that declares the image, ports, and resource requirements.
The container image's Dockerfile used to build it.
questions.correct_rationale: A task definition is the versioned declaration of image, ports, and resources that task runs reference; changing it does not rebuild the image.
distractor_rationales: Cluster configuration governs infrastructure, not the service's runtime declaration.
A target group routes traffic and holds no image or resource settings.
The Dockerfile builds the image; the requirement excludes rebuilding it.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options configure infrastructure, routing, or the build instead of the runtime declaration.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: A build pipeline reuses one mutable tag, 'prod', for every build, and an old image was silently overwritten by a broken build, leaving production deployments unpinnable. Which ECR setting prevents tags from being overwritten?
options: Move the registry to a private Region with restricted access
Create a lifecycle policy that deletes old image tags nightly from the repository.
Enable image tag immutability so a tag cannot be pushed twice.
Disable image pulls for repository tags older than one week.
questions.correct_rationale: Tag immutability rejects pushes that would overwrite an existing tag, so every tag refers to one unchanging image.
distractor_rationales: Region placement and access rules do not change tag semantics.
A lifecycle policy deletes images; it does not prevent overwrites.
Pull restrictions affect reading images, not writing over tags.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options delete, relocate, or restrict reading instead of preventing overwrites.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Prepare application artifacts to be deployed to AWS
questions.question: A platform team defines infrastructure in a programming language they already use, with the tool synthesizing deployable templates from the code. Which tool fits?
options: Hand-edited JSON sent to a support engineer for deployment.
A shared spreadsheet of resources maintained by hand by the operations team.
The AWS CDK, which synthesizes CloudFormation templates from code in familiar languages.
Screenshots of the architecture maintained with the code.
questions.correct_rationale: The CDK defines infrastructure in programming languages and synthesizes CloudFormation templates for deployment.
distractor_rationales: Hand-edited files through a human gateway add error and delay.
A spreadsheet is not executable infrastructure.
Screenshots describe nothing deployable.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options are not executable infrastructure as code.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: A team's regression suite lags behind new features: writing test cases for each change takes days. The team wants AI assistance generating test cases and automating repetitive test execution from the codebase. Which tool fits?
options: A load-testing tool pointed at production environments during peak traffic.
A larger fleet of manual QA contractors writing handwritten test scripts.
Q Developer's test generation and automation assistance.
A static password rotation policy applied to every developer account.
questions.correct_rationale: Amazon Q Developer assists with generating tests and automating repetitive testing work inside the development environment.
distractor_rationales: Production load tests measure capacity, not feature correctness.
More contractors scale the manual process rather than automating it.
Password rotation is unrelated to test coverage.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options scale manual work, test the wrong property, or change unrelated security hygiene.

docLinks.title: Chatting with Amazon Q Developer about code

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: A build runs unit and integration tests, and the team wants pass/fail counts per test case surfaced in the build's output and tracked across builds. Which CodeBuild capability fits?
options: Reading the raw build log line by line to find which test cases failed in each run.
A chat message posted by the build script's final step with a pass or fail summary and the name of the run.
Test reporting in CodeBuild, which parses test result files and shows per-case outcomes in the build.
Raising the build's compute type to a larger instance size so the full test suite finishes faster.
questions.correct_rationale: CodeBuild's test reporting parses standard result files and reports per-test outcomes across builds.
distractor_rationales: Raw logs require hand-reading and give no cross-build tracking.
A chat message carries no per-case structure.
Instance size changes speed, not reporting.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options broadcast, hand-read, or accelerate instead of structuring test results.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement and automate application testing in AWS environments
questions.question: A stack change touches a database and a queue. The team must preview exactly what will change and approve it before anything is applied. Which CloudFormation mechanism fits?
options: Deploy to production directly and roll back on failure
Delete the stack and recreate it with the new template
A change set showing proposed changes, applied only after review.
Rename the stack and hope conflicts resolve
questions.correct_rationale: A change set renders the diff a template update would cause and applies it only when reviewed and executed.
distractor_rationales: Direct deploys skip the preview entirely.
Recreating the stack destroys and rebuilds live resources.
Renaming has no bearing on the change review.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options destroy, skip review, or gesture at the problem.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A serverless API's function is invoked by API Gateway. Releases must shift a small percentage of traffic to the new version, hold there while error metrics are checked, then continue — with automatic rollback if errors rise. The compute must stay Lambda. Which mechanism fits?
options: Increasing the function's reserved concurrency and redeploying the function.
Redeploy the function with a new name and update the API integration manually.
A CodeDeploy Lambda deployment with a canary traffic-shifting configuration and alarm-based rollback
Publish a new layer version and let functions adopt it at their own pace.
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy supports traffic-shifting deployments for Lambda versions with canary or linear configurations and automatic rollback on CloudWatch alarms.
distractor_rationales: Concurrency changes capacity, not release safety.
A manual rename-and-repoint has no percentage shifting or automatic rollback.
Layers ship dependencies; they do not shift traffic between function versions.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options rename, resize, or ship dependencies instead of shifting traffic.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A stack update fails partway through applying a template change. The team requires that the stack return to its previous working state automatically rather than stay half-updated. Which behavior fits?
options: The stack deletes itself to prevent any configuration drift afterward.
The failed update leaves resources in place for manual repair afterward.
CloudFormation rolls the stack back to the last known good state.
CloudFormation retries the failed resource until it succeeds indefinitely.
questions.correct_rationale: On a failed update CloudFormation rolls the stack back to the previous known good state by default.
distractor_rationales: Self-deletion destroys working resources on failure.
A half-updated stack is precisely the state the requirement excludes.
Infinite retries are not the failure behavior.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options leave damage, destroy the stack, or retry forever.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A web app on Elastic Beanstalk deploys to a fleet behind a load balancer. Some releases change the host environment's dependencies, and the team wants those releases deployed without any user hitting a partially updated instance. Which deployment policy fits?
options: Manual weekly deployment windows agreed with the operations team.
All-at-once, the fastest deployment policy for small fleets.
Rolling in place across existing instances, so capacity dips during each batch.
Rolling with additional batch: new instances launch before old ones retire.
questions.correct_rationale: Rolling with additional batch brings up fresh instances on the new version before retiring old ones, so no user lands on a half-updated host.
distractor_rationales: Manual windows are a schedule, not a policy that protects users.
All-at-once updates everything at once, maximizing exposure to a bad release.
In-place rolling reuses hosts whose environment dependencies change mid-flight, serving users from partially updated hosts.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options maximize exposure, reuse dirty hosts, or substitute a calendar for a policy.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A containerized service on ECS must cut over between the old and new task set with traffic moved at once, and the old task set must stay warm to serve if the new one fails health checks. Which deployment type fits?
options: A cron job that restarts the tasks nightly with the stated behavior unchanged.
An ECS rolling update that replaces tasks gradually with the deployment configuration unchanged.
Deleting the service and creating it with the new task definition with the service's behavior unchanged.
CodeDeploy blue/green deployment for ECS, shifting traffic to the new task set with the old set kept for rollback.
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy's blue/green for ECS provisions the replacement task set, shifts traffic, and keeps the original task set available for rollback.
distractor_rationales: Nightly restarts are not a deployment strategy with rollback.
A rolling update replaces tasks in place gradually rather than cutting over with a warm old set.
Deleting the service drops traffic entirely.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options roll in place, drop traffic, or restart on a timer.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Deploy code by using AWS continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) services
questions.question: A team defines its serverless application in a SAM template and wants a single command flow that packages the artifacts and deploys the stack to an environment. Which tooling fits?
options: Screenshotting the architecture into an internal wiki with the stated behavior unchanged.
Copy-pasting the template into the console resource by resource by hand.
Emailing the template to a colleague with console access with the stated behavior unchanged.
The SAM CLI's build and deploy commands, which package artifacts and deploy the template as a stack.
questions.correct_rationale: The SAM CLI builds and packages the application's artifacts and deploys the template as a CloudFormation stack in one flow.
distractor_rationales: Documentation screenshots deploy nothing.
Manual console work invites drift from the template.
Emailing code is not a deployment pipeline.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options hand-deploy, email, or document instead of using the CLI flow.

docLinks.title: What is the AWS SAM framework?

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: A team's traces are voluminous and expensive, yet during incidents they lack traces for the specific requests that failed. Which X-Ray mechanism matches both needs?
options: Disabling all tracing outside the declared incident windows.
Adding a CloudWatch alarm on the error counts.
Raising every function's log level to DEBUG everywhere.
Sampling rules keeping traces for failed or slow requests.
questions.correct_rationale: Sampling rules decide which requests are traced — keeping traces of interest such as failures while cutting routine volume.
distractor_rationales: Turning tracing off removes exactly the evidence incidents need.
An alarm restates symptom counts and adds no request-level evidence.
Debug logging adds text volume without trace structure.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options remove evidence, add unstructured volume, or restate counts.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: A security tool must receive application log events in near-real time for its own analysis, without the applications writing anywhere except CloudWatch Logs, and without polling the log groups. Which mechanism forwards the events?
options: A scheduled Lambda that reads the log group contents on a timer.
A nightly export of the log groups to S3 with the bucket's settings unchanged.
The applications posting each log line to the security tool directly
A subscription filter on the log groups, streaming matching log events to the security tool's stream.
questions.correct_rationale: Subscription filters push log events in near-real time from CloudWatch Logs to destinations such as Kinesis streams.
distractor_rationales: A scheduled reader is polling with delay, which the requirement excludes.
Nightly export is neither real time nor continuous.
Direct dual-writing couples the applications to the tool and defeats the single logging path.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options batch, couple, or poll instead of streaming events.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: One integration partner's client receives 429 responses while all other clients work. The API has no per-client settings yet, and the partner's legitimate burst traffic should be allowed at a higher rate than the default while abusive clients stay throttled. Which mechanism fits?
options: Retrying the partner's failed requests inside the API automatically.
Disabling throttling on the whole stage so no client is limited.
Blocking the partner's IP range at the network firewall perimeter.
A usage plan with higher throttle limits attached to the partner's API key.
questions.correct_rationale: Usage plans attach per-client throttle and quota limits to API keys, letting the partner's burst allowance rise without changing everyone else's.
distractor_rationales: The API retrying on the caller's behalf does not address rate limiting.
Disabling stage throttling removes protection for every client.
IP blocking neither identifies the client at the API layer nor grants a higher allowance.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options remove limits, block at the wrong layer, or retry blindly.

docLinks.title: Usage plans and API keys in API Gateway

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Assist in a root cause analysis
questions.question: A CodeBuild project starts failing at the build phase. The team must find the failing command and its error output first. Where should they look?
options: The CloudFront distribution's access logs for the content delivery.
The service's production dashboard for the deployed environment's health.
The IAM policy documents attached to the build role in IAM.
The build logs in CodeBuild, showing every command's output in order.
questions.correct_rationale: CodeBuild records each build command's output in the build logs, ordered by phase, which is the first place a failed command appears.
distractor_rationales: Distribution access logs describe content delivery, not builds.
A production dashboard reflects runtime behavior, not the build.
IAM policies define permissions, not build output.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options look at runtime, permissions, or delivery instead of the build log.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: Downstream complaints say orders are slow, but the worker fleet reports healthy CPU and the dead-letter queue is empty. The queue's oldest-message age keeps climbing during the day and recovers overnight. What does this indicate?
options: The workers are failing silently, and messages are being retried.
Messages are being lost in transit, since the DLQ is empty.
The queue's server-side encryption is too slow for the workload.
Inflow outpaces consumption at peak, so processing lags without failures.
questions.correct_rationale: Rising oldest-message age with healthy workers and an empty DLQ means inflow outpaces consumption at peak — a throughput lag, not a failure loop.
distractor_rationales: Failing workers would show redeliveries and DLQ movement.
An empty DLQ does not imply loss; it implies no message exhausted its delivery attempts.
Queue encryption does not produce time-of-day patterns.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options infer loss, blame encryption, or claim failures the signals contradict.

docLinks.title: Available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: A target behind an application load balancer was restarted into a bad state, and the load balancer kept sending it user traffic for minutes. What mechanism removes an unhealthy target from rotation automatically?
options: The target group's health checks, which stop routing to failing targets.
A CloudWatch alarm that emails the on-call engineer.
Higher connection idle timeouts configured on the listener.
Disabling sticky sessions on the target group's configuration.
questions.correct_rationale: Target group health checks probe each target and the load balancer stops routing to targets that fail, removing bad instances from rotation.
distractor_rationales: An emailed engineer responds after users already hit the bad target.
Listener timeouts change connection behavior, not routing health.
Sticky sessions affect request affinity, not health routing.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options notify late, alter timeouts, or change affinity instead of routing on health.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Apply logging, monitoring, and observability best practices
questions.question: A service logs structured error events, and operations must be paged when a specific error signature appears more than a few times in minutes. Which mechanism turns the log pattern into an alarm?
options: A second log group receiving the same events for redundancy and safety.
A manual review rota over the log groups each day.
A higher log retention period configured on the log group.
A metric filter counting matching events, with an alarm on the resulting metric.
questions.correct_rationale: A metric filter converts matching log events into a metric, and an alarm on that metric pages when the signature exceeds the threshold.
distractor_rationales: Duplicating log groups adds cost without detection.
A review rota is neither real time nor automatic.
Retention changes how long logs live, not how they alarm.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options review, retain, or duplicate instead of converting logs to metrics.

docLinks.title: Monitoring log data with metric filters

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Optimize applications by using AWS services and features
questions.question: A subscription service serves video lessons from CloudFront. Everyone with the URL watches for free once links leak, and the business requires links that work only for the paying subscriber and expire. Which mechanism fits?
options: Compressing the videos so they load faster for everyone.
A larger cache TTL so content serves faster.
An origin access identity granting public read on the origin bucket.
Signed CloudFront URLs expiring after the subscriber session.
questions.correct_rationale: Signed URLs restrict content delivery to authenticated subscribers and can carry an expiry, so leaked links stop working.
distractor_rationales: Compression changes size, not authorization.
Cache TTL changes delivery speed, not who may watch.
Public read on the origin makes content universally accessible.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options tune speed or openness while the requirement is restricted, expiring access.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Optimize applications by using AWS services and features
questions.question: Tracing every request through a high-traffic API costs more than the team can justify, yet the on-call team must still see traces when latency crosses a slow threshold or errors occur. Which configuration balances both?
options: Sampling the first request of every hour for the trace with the tracing behavior unchanged.
Tracing every request and paying the cost with the stated behavior unchanged.
Turning tracing off and relying on log text with the logging behavior unchanged.
Sampling rules that trace a small baseline share of requests plus all requests that exceed latency or error conditions.
questions.correct_rationale: Sampling rules combine a low baseline rate with unconditional tracing of anomalous requests, cutting cost while keeping the traces incidents need.
distractor_rationales: Hourly sampling captures nothing relevant to a specific slow or failing request.
Tracing everything is the cost being cut.
No tracing leaves incidents blind by design.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options pay in full, go blind, or sample arbitrary requests.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Optimize applications by using AWS services and features
questions.question: An API endpoint returns the same catalog payload for most callers for minutes at a time, and the backend computation behind it is expensive. Which feature serves repeated responses without invoking the backend every time?
options: Removing the endpoint's request validation settings entirely with the API's configuration unchanged.
A bigger Lambda function memory setting so the payload is computed faster.
An SQS queue placed in front of the endpoint to absorb the incoming requests.
Stage-level API caching, which stores responses and serves them within the TTL.
questions.correct_rationale: Stage-level caching stores integration responses and serves repeated requests from the cache for the configured time, sparing the backend.
distractor_rationales: Validation guards requests and has no effect on response reuse.
A faster function still runs for every request.
A queue defers work; it does not serve repeated reads.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options speed the backend, defer work, or guard input instead of reusing responses.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A consumer application had a parsing bug from 09:00 to 11:00, during which it skipped incoming clickstream records. The team must reprocess exactly the records from that window, without the producers re-sending anything. Which Kinesis capability fits?
options: Resend the affected records by replaying them from the producers' local log files.
Increase the stream's data retention so a repaired consumer can still read the skipped window.
Create a new stream and have producers duplicate all events into both streams during incidents.
Export the shard data to S3 every hour and query it with Athena after each incident.
questions.correct_rationale: Extending retention keeps records readable after the normal consumption window, so a repaired consumer can read the skipped window without producers re-sending.
distractor_rationales: Producer-side replay requires the producers to have retained their own logs and duplicates events at the source.
Dual-stream duplication doubles producer cost permanently and still needs a recovery path.
Hourly S3 exports create a separate copy for analytics and do not give the stream consumer a way to reprocess in place.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options re-send data at the source, duplicate streams, or build a copy pipeline instead of extending retention.

docLinks.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams key concepts

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A payment service publishes many event types to one bus. The fraud function must run only for declined-payment events, the ledger function only for settled-payment events, and consumers must be added without publisher changes. Which mechanism fits?
options: An SQS queue holding all events, with each function polling and skipping irrelevant ones.
A single EventBridge rule that targets one function, which fans events out to the others in code.
An SNS topic whose subscription filter policies select each function's event types.
EventBridge rules whose event patterns match each event type and route to the matching target.
questions.correct_rationale: EventBridge rules match events by pattern and route each type to its own target, so consumers change without touching the publisher.
distractor_rationales: A shared queue cannot route by type and delivers each message to one consumer.
A single fan-out function couples every consumer into one code path, which adding a consumer must not do.
SNS filter policies select within one subscription model but the routing decision here belongs on the bus where events already flow.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options couple consumers in code, move routing to a different bus, or lose the multi-consumer delivery.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A nightly workflow must run three independent data-processing jobs in parallel and start the reporting job only after all three finish, treating any job failure as a workflow failure. The team wants no custom polling or counters. Which integration fits?
options: Start the three jobs with fire-and-forget integrations and use a Lambda function to poll their status.
Start the three jobs with run-job integrations that wait for completion, then continue to the reporting state.
Run the three jobs from a scheduled script and start the reporting job with a CloudWatch alarm.
Put the three jobs in sequence so each finishes before the next begins, then report.
questions.correct_rationale: Run-job service integrations with the wait-for-completion pattern hold parallel branches until each job finishes, and Parallel states join when all branches succeed.
distractor_rationales: Fire-and-forget plus a polling function reintroduces the custom polling the requirement excludes.
An alarm-based start has no completion barrier linking the three jobs to the report.
Sequential execution removes the parallelism the workflow requires.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options poll, alarm, or serialize instead of using parallel wait-for-completion branches.

docLinks.title: Wait for a callback with the task token

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: A Lambda function's handler must call five downstream services in a fixed order, retrying each step on failure with its own backoff and branching to a cleanup step on any final failure. Which approach replaces the hand-written retry and branching code?
options: A Step Functions state machine whose task states define the order, retry rules, and catch branches.
A try/except block around all five calls that retries the whole sequence from the start each time.
An SQS queue between each pair of services so every step retries through its own dead-letter queue.
A cron rule that re-invokes the whole handler on a schedule until every step has succeeded.
questions.correct_rationale: Step Functions task states declare per-step retry and catch behavior, so the sequence and its error branches are defined rather than coded.
distractor_rationales: Retrying the whole sequence re-runs completed steps and cannot branch per step.
Queues between every pair add polling infrastructure and still lack a declared cleanup path.
Cron re-invocation restarts the workflow instead of resuming the failed step.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options retry coarsely, add queue hops without declared branches, or restart the whole workflow.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: An EventBridge rule delivers order events to a target that accepts only three fields, while the original event carries dozens. Which feature reshapes the event before delivery without adding processing code?
options: An input transformer that defines variables from the original event's JSON paths and sends the template output to the target.
A second rule with a narrower event pattern that filters which fields of the original event are carried through to the target.
A Lambda function placed between the rule and the target that copies the three needed fields into a brand new event.
An archive of the original events that the target replays later in smaller batches with fewer fields.
questions.correct_rationale: The input transformer builds a custom payload from JSON-path variables of the original event, so the target receives just the fields it accepts.
distractor_rationales: A narrower pattern filters which events match, not which fields an event carries.
Inserting a Lambda adds processing code the team was told to avoid.
Archives store events for replay and change nothing about delivery shape.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options filter whole events, insert new processing code, or only store for replay.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A product-lookup API reads items from a DynamoDB table with eventually consistent reads at single-digit-millisecond latency, but the frontend needs microsecond reads and the team cannot rewrite the application's item calls. Which addition fits?
options: Provisioned read capacity raised on the table step by step until query responses arrive faster for users.
A Global Secondary Index on the table's lookup attribute to shorten every query path the application takes to the item.
An ElastiCache cluster that the application code populates from the table on a schedule, with new read logic added to check the cache first.
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), an in-memory cache that brings eventually consistent reads to microseconds without application changes.
questions.correct_rationale: DAX is a DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache that reduces eventually consistent read times from milliseconds to microseconds, requiring no application rewrites.
distractor_rationales: More read capacity raises throughput limits without changing response latency.
An index speeds query targeting but not item-read latency to microseconds.
Populating ElastiCache on a schedule requires new application code and serves stale data.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add indexes, add a cache that needs new code, or add capacity without latency change.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: The application's next release needs multi-row ACID transactions, SQL joins across entities, and schema-enforced foreign keys. Which data store provides all three natively?
options: Amazon DynamoDB, whose schemaless items scale without fixed column definitions.
Amazon RDS, whose relational engines run SQL transactions, joins, and constraint enforcement.
Amazon S3, whose objects organize data under keys and prefixes.
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator, which caches existing item reads in memory.
questions.correct_rationale: Relational engines on Amazon RDS provide ACID transactions, joins, and foreign-key constraints as core SQL features.
distractor_rationales: DynamoDB items are schemaless and do not enforce foreign keys.
S3 objects carry no relational schema, joins, or constraints.
DAX accelerates reads and adds no transactional or relational features.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options lack schema enforcement, relational joins, or any transactional role.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: An application must convert written notifications into spoken audio for a phone-based interface, with no machine learning expertise on the team. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Polly, which turns text into natural-sounding speech.
Amazon Transcribe, which turns recorded speech into text.
Amazon Comprehend, which analyzes text for meaning and entities.
Amazon Rekognition, which analyzes images and video.
questions.correct_rationale: Polly is a text-to-speech service: it takes written text and returns spoken audio.
distractor_rationales: Transcribe works in the opposite direction, speech to text.
Comprehend analyzes text; it produces no audio.
Rekognition processes images and video, not text or speech.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options transcribe, analyze, or classify instead of synthesizing speech.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A social app lets users upload images publicly. Policy requires that uploaded images are screened for explicit or unsafe content before they appear, with a managed API rather than a hand-built classifier. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Rekognition's content moderation APIs, which detect unsafe images.
Amazon Textract, which extracts printed text and structure from document images.
Amazon Comprehend, which analyzes text documents for meaning.
Amazon Transcribe, which converts speech recordings into text.
questions.correct_rationale: Rekognition's moderation APIs classify images for explicit and unsafe content so the app can block them before publication.
distractor_rationales: Textract reads documents, not safety.
Comprehend analyzes text, and the uploads are images.
Transcribe works on audio, which is the wrong media type.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options analyze documents, text, or audio instead of screening images.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Use data stores during application development
questions.question: A web application runs on a fleet behind a load balancer. Users are logged out when the load balancer moves their next request to a different server, because session data is stored on the instance that first served them. Which pattern fixes this?
options: Store sessions on each instance's local disk and copy them across instances hourly.
Enable sticky sessions so each user stays on their original instance permanently.
Store session state in an ElastiCache cluster that every instance reads and writes.
Store session data in the application's container image and rebuild per session.
questions.correct_rationale: A shared in-memory cache decouples session state from any single instance, so any server can serve any user.
distractor_rationales: Hourly local-disk copies still lose sessions on failure and serve stale state between copies.
Sticky sessions mask the statelessness problem, reduce load-balancing flexibility, and reset when the instance dies.
Sessions in an image are baked read-only build artifacts and cannot hold per-user runtime state.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options pin users, copy state late, or treat sessions as build artifacts.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Develop code for AWS Lambda
questions.question: Two Lambda functions share one database but need different credentials: one read-only, one read-write. Credentials must rotate automatically and each function must reach only its own secret. Which approach fits?
options: Store two Secrets Manager secrets with automatic rotation, scoping each function's IAM access to its own secret.
Store both credentials in one shared secret that both functions read, and parse the right pair at runtime.
Store the credentials as plaintext environment variables configured on each function, with rotation handled by a manual runbook each quarter.
Store one credential and grant both functions read-write access to it, simplifying operations at the security team's expense.
questions.correct_rationale: Per-secret IAM scoping gives each function only its own credential, and Secrets Manager rotation keeps both current.
distractor_rationales: A combined secret hands both functions whichever credential they parse, breaking least privilege.
Plaintext environment variables have no rotation and expose the credential in configuration.
A shared read-write credential removes the read-only boundary the design requires.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options merge, expose, or over-share credentials instead of scoping per function.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A podcast platform must generate searchable text and captions from uploaded audio episodes automatically. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Comprehend, which extracts entities from existing text.
Amazon Polly, which converts text into speech audio.
Amazon Rekognition, which analyzes video content for labels.
Amazon Transcribe, which converts speech audio into text.
questions.correct_rationale: Transcribe converts recorded speech into transcribed text, which captions and search both need.
distractor_rationales: Comprehend analyzes text that already exists.
Polly synthesizes speech; the platform needs the reverse direction.
Rekognition labels images and video frames, not speech.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options synthesize, label, or analyze instead of transcribing audio.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: An expense application must pull the vendor, date, and total amounts out of photographed paper receipts so users do not type them by hand. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Textract, which extracts text and structured data from document images.
Amazon Rekognition, which detects labels, objects, and unsafe content in images.
Amazon Comprehend, which finds entities and sentiment in plain text that is already typed.
Amazon Transcribe, which converts recorded speech audio into a text transcript.
questions.correct_rationale: Textract extracts printed text and form fields from document images such as receipts.
distractor_rationales: Rekognition sees objects and labels; it does not return structured receipt fields.
Comprehend needs existing text; the receipts are images.
Transcribe works on audio, not paper.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options label, parse text they are not given, or process audio.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Develop code for applications that are hosted on AWS
questions.question: A central bus delivers the same event JSON to an inventory system that expects a compact custom payload and an audit store that expects a different shape. The publishers must not change, and no per-target transformation function may be added. Which feature fits?
options: Publishing a separate event per target from the publishers, each in the target's format.
A shared transformation function between the bus and every target that switches on the target name.
EventBridge input transformers, which reshape the event into each target's expected format at the target.
Storing the event in S3 and sending each target a link to interpret as it prefers.
questions.correct_rationale: Input transformers configure the delivered payload per target on the rule, reshaping events without extra functions or publisher changes.
distractor_rationales: Per-target publisher events couple publishers to every consumer's format and change with each new target.
A shared transformation function is the per-target function component the requirement excludes.
A link to stored events pushes the format problem to every target without solving it.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options add the excluded component, couple publishers, or defer the transformation to targets.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A bucket must be readable by the company's applications through their VPC endpoint, while the same bucket stays unreachable from any other network path, including the public internet. Which control expresses this?
options: A public bucket whose objects stay unreadable in practice because outsiders do not know the objects' key names.
A security group rule that allows the bucket's IP range from the application subnets.
A bucket policy condition that allows access only when requests arrive through the VPC endpoint's identifier.
A NAT gateway that routes the applications' traffic to the bucket's public endpoint.
questions.correct_rationale: A condition on the source VPC endpoint lets the bucket policy allow exactly the endpoint's traffic and deny everything else.
distractor_rationales: A public bucket is reachable by anyone who learns the names; secrecy is not access control.
Security groups filter traffic to instances, not requests to the bucket, and IP ranges do not identify the endpoint path.
A NAT gateway sends traffic over the public path the requirement forbids.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options filter the wrong layer, rely on secrecy, or force the public path.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: Developers in one AWS account must work daily on resources in another account, and the security team refuses to create duplicate IAM users in the target account. Which mechanism grants the access?
options: Duplicate IAM users in the target account, with long-lived keys handed to each developer.
A cross-account IAM role in the target account that the developers assume through AWS STS for temporary credentials.
The developers' home-account access keys pasted into the target account's environment variables.
An IAM group in the home account that mirrors the target account's permissions.
questions.correct_rationale: Assuming a cross-account role through STS issues short-lived credentials for the target account without creating any IAM users there.
distractor_rationales: Duplicate users recreate exactly the identity sprawl the security team refused.
Home-account keys pasted elsewhere leak long-lived credentials and gain no target permissions.
A home-account group has no authority over resources in another account.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options recreate user sprawl, leak long-lived keys, or have no cross-account authority.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A data-owning account must let one application in another account decrypt with its customer-managed key. Access must require agreement from both accounts' security teams, each controlling its own side. Which access design fits?
options: The other account creates its own KMS key and encrypts a copy of the data independently.
The data owner emails the key's plaintext key material to the other account's administrators so they can import it.
The key policy names the other account, whose administrators then delegate the key to the application through IAM.
The key policy allows every principal account-wide, and the other account filters access in its applications.
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account key access is split: the key policy grants the external account, whose IAM then decides which of its principals may assume that grant.
distractor_rationales: A second independent key does not let the other account decrypt the existing ciphertext.
Shared key material is a permanent compromise of the encryption model and a security incident.
An account-wide allow with application-side filtering has no enforced control on the key itself.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options leak key material, duplicate the key, or remove the key-side control.

docLinks.title: Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A web tier behind an application load balancer still accepts plaintext HTTP alongside HTTPS, and some clients never upgrade. Traffic must be forced to TLS for every request, and the certificate must renew on its own. Which configuration fits?
options: A self-signed certificate installed on each target instance and renewed by an engineer's script.
An ACM certificate on an HTTPS listener with a modern policy, and an HTTP listener that redirects to HTTPS.
A security group that blocks port 443 at the load balancer entirely, so clients have no way to negotiate TLS.
TLS termination left disabled, so encrypted traffic passes through to targets unmodified and unexamined.
questions.correct_rationale: The ACM-backed HTTPS listener terminates TLS with an automatic-renewing certificate, and the redirect-only HTTP listener forces every plaintext request onto it.
distractor_rationales: Self-signed certificates on instances are untrusted by clients and reintroduce manual renewal.
Blocking port 443 blocks TLS itself, not plaintext.
Disabling termination removes the TLS the requirement mandates.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options break trust, block TLS, or remove encryption instead of enforcing it.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: Internal services must authenticate each other with mutual TLS using certificates that name the company, not a public authority. No public CA interaction or per-certificate purchase may be involved. Which managed capability fits?
options: Certificates purchased individually from a public certificate authority for every internal service that needs one.
AWS Private CA, which issues and manages certificates from a private hierarchy the company controls.
Self-signed certificates generated separately by each service and exchanged between teams over email.
SSH keys shared between the services through a plain configuration file.
questions.correct_rationale: A private CA issues certificates for internal identities under a company-controlled hierarchy, enabling mutual TLS without any public authority.
distractor_rationales: Public CA certificates are for publicly trusted endpoints and add per-certificate cost and process that internal mTLS does not need.
Emailed self-signed certificates are untrusted and unmanaged.
SSH keys are a different mechanism from certificate-based mutual TLS.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options buy public trust, share untrusted certificates, or use the wrong credential type.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A developer's role shows an Allow for both the S3 action and the resource in its identity policy, yet requests still fail with access denied. Review of all attached policies reveals one statement denying that action. Which evaluation rule explains the failure?
options: An explicit deny in any policy overrides every Allow in the evaluation.
The most recently modified policy statement wins the evaluation.
Allow and deny statements cancel out, and the request is retried later.
Resource policies are evaluated before identity policies, so the deny is ignored.
questions.correct_rationale: Within IAM's evaluation logic, an explicit deny terminates the decision, so one deny statement defeats any number of Allow statements.
distractor_rationales: Evaluation is not time-based; modification order plays no role.
Deny and allow do not cancel into a retry; the deny simply wins.
Both policy types contribute to one evaluation, and the deny governs across them.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options invent recency, cancellation, or ordering rules that do not exist.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: A platform stores non-secret configuration as String parameters and database credentials as encrypted parameters. Compliance requires the encrypted parameters to use a key whose policy the platform team controls. Which parameter type and key choice fit?
options: String parameters with the values encoded in base64 for obscurity.
SecureString parameters encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key whose policy the team edits.
SecureString parameters encrypted with the default AWS-managed key, whose policy the team cannot edit.
Plaintext String parameters stored in a bucket with bucket policies.
questions.correct_rationale: SecureString is the encrypted parameter type, and choosing a customer-managed KMS key puts the key policy under the platform team's control.
distractor_rationales: Base64 is an encoding, not encryption, and String parameters are not encrypted.
The AWS-managed key cannot have its policy edited by the team, which the requirement names.
A bucket of plaintext strings is not an encrypted parameter store.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options encode instead of encrypting, use a key the team cannot control, or leave the store.

docLinks.title: What is Systems Manager Parameter Store?

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: A team adopts AI-assisted coding and must review every generated change for security defects before merging, with the review inside their existing workflow. Which capability fits?
options: Amazon Q Developer's security review of code in the development workflow.
A manual checklist that reviewers memorize for each pull request.
Disabling AI assistance so no generated code enters the repository.
Rotating the developers' CLI credentials more frequently than the current schedule.
questions.correct_rationale: Q Developer's security review flags defects in code — including AI-generated changes — inside the development workflow.
distractor_rationales: A memorized checklist is the manual process the tool replaces and scales poorly.
Disabling AI assistance addresses adoption policy, not review of the code that exists.
Credential rotation is unrelated to code defect detection.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options memorize, ban, or rotate instead of reviewing the code.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A content app lets anonymous visitors browse a free catalog, and signed-in subscribers unlock premium items. Both flows read the same S3 content through temporary AWS credentials. Which identity pool setup fits?
options: One role shared by everyone, with the application filtering premium content before each display.
Two roles: one for unauthenticated guests scoped to the catalog, one for subscribers scoped to premium.
A single bucket policy that inspects each caller's subscription status before granting object reads.
Hard-coding the premium objects' URLs into each subscriber's device during registration and revoking them later by hand.
questions.correct_rationale: Identity pools issue unauthenticated guests and authenticated users different roles, so each session receives credentials scoped to its tier.
distractor_rationales: A shared role cannot hold two scopes, and client-side filtering hides content without protecting it.
Bucket policies cannot evaluate a caller's subscription status in the application's business sense.
Hard-coded URLs are static credentials by another name and leak instantly.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options share one role, filter client-side, or hard-code access.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: A user pool protects a financial dashboard, and the security team requires that sign-in verifies a second factor the user holds, with the policy enforced at sign-in rather than by the application. Which user pool capability fits?
options: A longer password-expiration cycle applied to the pool's users at their next sign-in.
A stronger password-complexity policy applied to every user in the pool.
Checking the user's IP address against a spreadsheet at each sign-in.
Multi-factor authentication on the user pool, required at sign-in for the protected users.
questions.correct_rationale: User pool MFA challenges for a second factor during sign-in, enforced by the service before tokens are issued.
distractor_rationales: Password expiration changes rotation habits, not authentication strength at sign-in.
Password complexity strengthens one factor; the requirement is a second factor.
Spreadsheet IP checks are outside the sign-in flow and trivially stale.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options tune the first factor, check location by hand, or change rotation instead of adding a factor.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify and mitigate security risks associated with using and integrating AI services into application development
questions.question: An audit requires complete model invocation records, and privacy requires that personal information customers type never appears in those records. Which configuration satisfies both?
options: Storing invocation records in the application's own database with customer passwords hashed.
Invocation logging disabled so nothing personal can be recorded, resuming it after the audit.
A manual scrubbing job that edits the log store nightly to strip personal information after it is already recorded.
Invocation logging enabled, with a guardrail that redacts personal information from prompts and responses before records are stored.
questions.correct_rationale: Guardrail redaction strips personal information from prompts and responses while invocation logging keeps the complete record the audit needs.
distractor_rationales: A self-managed store is not the service's invocation record and hashing passwords addresses a different field.
Disabling logging fails the audit requirement outright and only pauses the exposure.
Nightly scrubbing leaves personal information in the store between runs and after retention copies.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options abandon the audit, scrub late, or rebuild the record outside the service.

docLinks.title: Model invocation logging in Amazon Bedrock

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement encryption and manage sensitive data by using AWS services
questions.question: An internal certificate used for service-to-service mutual TLS may have leaked. The security team must make clients stop trusting that certificate immediately, without reissuing the rest of the hierarchy. Which mechanism fits?
options: Issue a second certificate with the same identity and hope clients prefer it.
Wait for the certificate's expiration date to arrive and pass without action.
Revoke the certificate through the private CA so status checks by clients reject it.
Delete the whole private CA so every certificate it ever issued stops working at once.
questions.correct_rationale: Revocation through the CA marks that certificate untrusted for clients that check certificate status, leaving the rest of the hierarchy intact.
distractor_rationales: A second same-identity certificate does not withdraw the first; clients may accept either.
Waiting for expiry leaves the possibly leaked certificate valid for the remaining lifetime.
Deleting the CA breaks every certificate it ever issued, far beyond the one leak.
questions.distractor_summary: The wrong options wait, add a competing certificate, or destroy the whole hierarchy.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms for applications and AWS services
questions.question: An S3 upload must invoke a function in the same account. The security team requires that the function can be invoked only by this bucket's event source, with the invocation permission scoped in one auditable place. Which mechanism fits?
